text:
During our most recent monthly community AMA, a community member asked if the team is actively negotiating with other mainstream Web2 animated IPs for upcoming TokenFi Launchpad releases.

Our Core Advisor, B (@100bviking), provided the following response:

---

We stopped actively engaging with partner projects using the airdrop-to-holders model as has been previously communicated a few times in the past, and we’ve actually turned down or ignored several projects that have reached out to cooperate with us based on this kind of arrangement.
This was a difficult decision for us, but we made it after paying careful attention to the community and seeing a vocal majority being in favor of stopping this kind of partnerships. We’ll communicate if this changes in the future.

In the meanwhile, we’re focused on deepening our collaboration with existing partners while unlocking more value for Floki and TokenFi holders alongside their ecosystem.

For example, $RICE was the last project we had this kind of partnership with and there is so much going on with their ecosystem that I think people should be paying attention to.

Naturally, in a bear market nobody pays attention… but in a bull market it suddenly makes a lot of sense when price starts to trend up again.

The intersection of crypto and robotics is a very big, untapped market with massive potential. It’s hard to imagine a project with better potential to succeed in this sector than $RICE. Many might not have been paying attention, but they’ve been building hard, forming strategic partnerships, pursuing strategic educational outreach initiatives across the globe, etc.

Their token price action might not make it seem like it right now, but I think it’s going to be clear in hindsight that we delivered a winner to Floki and TokenFi holders with this one.

I should also add that Floki/TokenFi holders got a batch of $RICE airdrop last week, and another one should be due this week all things being equal. There is also quite a bit more of this coming to Floki and TokenFi holders in the future.

So again, we are unlikely to partner with a new project on this kind of initiative in line with our community’s wishes, but we are committed to actively supporting strong projects like RICE to help unlock the most value for our community and theirs!

---

appreciate the spotlight from the @arc team and the deeper look at what we're building with Pulsar.

for us, the opportunity with stablecoins starts with the everyday things people need their money to do. receive a payment from abroad, keep money in dollars or euros, send some home, pay for a subscription or use it while travelling

we see clear use cases around bringing global accounts to people across different regions, making payments easier and improving how people move between stablecoins and their accounts. the rates they get, the steps they go through and how easily they can use the money afterwards all matter

those needs are already there. our job is to make the experience simple enough that someone can use @PulsarMoneyApp without learning about chains, bridges or gas tokens along the way

this is a big part of why we chose Arc. @USDC-based network fees help us build around more predictable costs, and fast onchain settlement helps us give people clearer answers about what's happening with their money. the connection to @Circle's infrastructure also matters when bringing funds in from different networks

we're also working towards integrating StableFX into our currency conversion experience. better rates and a smoother experience across currencies are an important part of what we want to offer people whose income, spending and family are spread across borders

what excites us is how much room there is to make these everyday money experiences better and bring them to more people

excited to keep building this ONARC! 🔥

Local AI caught up way faster than anyone realizes. Sharing my thoughts having spent time in ML at Meta and dedicating the last year to getting smart on local AI.
1/ Barely anyone, not even hardcore AI power users, realizes how fast local models have caught up to the frontier. Qwen3.8 woke a few people up, but the most technical people are so frontier-pilled they've blinded themselves to the breakneck progress.
Meanwhile, normal users don't care about frontier intelligence at all. They want AI that gets the job done, but they have no idea what a local model is or how to run one.

text:
Listened back to this talk as I'm obv very bullish onchain options 

My take has been that HL will not attack options themselves and instead will wait on a builder / deployer to be successful, because they would either have to: 

1) hire aggressively
2) make an acquisition

This talk pretty much confirms my take. Building out options isn't an easy feat, and their team remains very lean.

Jeff points to HIP-4 and names options as the next big opportunity here. During the talk, he appealed to deployers multiple times to build on top of their infra and grab this market. 

There are lots of synergies here, as an options deployer gets access to HL's orderbooks making it easy for both traders and MMs to utilize and hedge against perp and spot positions. That's the real value unlock. 

So we'll likely see the same thing as has unfolded with @tradexyz and RWA perps: a cracked team builds out the options product on HIP-4 / connected to core writer, and distro + volume come from HL's frontend. 

Only a few teams to watch in this HL niche so far, and the question is how long it will take until a deployer on HL is successful.

Until major developments, teams already competing in this space like @DeriveXYZ and @paradex continue to lead the race, enjoying a first mover advantage

text:
老马的这条推暗含着一个重大转变，老马今天说以后Grok Bot这个agent产品层面会“挑最好的模型用”，不锁死自家模型。按具体任务选最合适的后端模型——文本推理可能用 Claude Opus 5.5，生图可能用 MidJourney，音频/音乐可能用 Suno，再加上其他领先 API。标准只有一个：哪种最可能给出最好结果，就用哪种。

重点是agent产品和模型路由，Bot是上层助手：能连账户、主动做事、跨工具执行；底层模型则按任务外接，不强制全走 xAI 自己的模型。当然不是xAI停掉 Grok 模型研发，但明显未来重心在Bot这个Agent层面上了。

这个思路是对的，与其大模型这个已是红海的领域疯狂卷，还不如去卷Agent这个自己更有好优势的领域。

这就是暗含了SpaceX在AI上未来的重点就是两个：
1）夯实最底层的算力中心、这是现金流业务，spacex有着极强的工程能力（每MW的建设成本能做到最低）；
2）抢占入口、基于X这个越来越活跃的社交平台、bot一开始天然就有一个无可比拟的分发渠道平台，不锁死自家大模型会让用户对bot的体验更好、更能留住用户。未来还能向其他大模型厂商卖更多算力。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
年初说大模型厂商各领风骚三五月，没有一家能长期领先甚至垄断，都是快速迭代、轮流坐庄。这不延迟几个月之后Gemini4终于发布了，Gemini 4 Argon (High) 的社区盲测表现很强，尤其在文本综合能力上直接登顶。不过今年市场经历过GPT5.5、5.6、6Astra，Claude fable 5.1、Opus 5.5 ，Grok 4的轮番轰炸，这还不算中国大模型的更高频的迭代，其实有点麻木了。

而且貌似AI主战场当下的焦点已不在模型本身而是转移到Agent上，Grok Bot、Meta Muse、OpenAI Dots等近期轮番上场，不断在推动这一点的迭代。其实谷歌做Agent也很有优势：有超大用户量、海量数据积累、强分发能力，这块发力应该也很有看头。

2月中在《资本开支的战争》推文里有聊过：”往下游看，越往用户端竞争越激烈，当然也是未来AI决胜的关键所在。 可以说大模型、在面向B端或者C端的Agent或者应用才是AI的王冠，但这一层面短期其实很难看出谁会成为最后真正的赢家，再很多时候都是交替领先” https://t.co/zEVlDF6sOr

text:
been hearing a lot of people say frontier labs are cooked bc their subscriptions don't make money. some quick things from the @SemiAnalysis_ piece that matter here:

- subs are ~10% of anthropic's revenue. yes they eat 40%+ of compute but they're not the business

- the business is the API. ~90% of revenue at ~90% est margins, mostly enterprise

- the sub is basically CAC. devs use claude code via sub, then their company buys the API. would be interesting to measure sub to enterprise conversion (ofc bigger risk is enterprises not tokenmaxxing)

- most people prob don't max their plan anyway (semi assumes ~20% avg utilization)

- the best models get tighter limits so the subsidy shrinks as usage moves up

so no, don't think Anthropic or OpenAI are cooked...
author: santiagoroel
quoted_text:
It doesn't make sense to say a subscription plan is worth $ X in isolation.

The way to think about subscriptions is that your monthly payment grants you some numbers of “credits”. Each (model, token type) combo consumes a different amount of credits. Because credit cost ratios can differ dramatically from API price ratios, the “value” of the same plan changes depending on what model and workload you’re running.

An independent application layer built on top of the IMD network, specifically designed for virtual influencers that can maintain the same identity over the long term. However, the project itself is not an official IMD product; it simply uses IMD’s publicly available tasks, verification, and agent workflows.

It solves one of the biggest problems with ordinary text-to-image or text-to-video generation: once you change the scene or switch models, the face, voice, and persona tend to drift. So the project aims to turn “a character” into a reusable specification: define the appearance, voice, personality, boundaries, and content direction first, then hand them over to different specialized agents to generate images, produce videos, write copy, and monitor data.

The product workflow consists of four steps:Describe → Validate → Approve → Operate

The specialized roles include Identity Architect, Visual Director, Content Room, Policy Guard, and Growth Analyst.

The current numbers displayed on the official website are 128 agents ready, 12 identities operating 24/7, 4,821 creative steps, and 37 active campaigns, with the content clearly marked as AI-generated.

The PMD token is currently mainly used for access and eligibility: holding 100,000 PMD unlocks free agent generation, and after wallet verification on Ethereum mainnet, the identity agent can be connected to the IMD swarm and launched.

If the IMD swarm can continue receiving tasks, this type of application layer already has an execution layer available, without needing to build and maintain an entire inference cluster itself.

Its main advantages are: personas can be reused across different formats, the system is connected to IMD’s payment / verification / launch process, and token holdings can be directly converted into generation credits.

Tether 遭遇美国审查

Tether 因伊朗相关网络使用 USDT 转移资金、涉嫌规避制裁，已经受到美国参议院调查，审查重点是公司的反洗钱和制裁合规措施。

美国参议院常设调查小组委员会的民主党调查人员发布报告，分析了 846 个因涉及伊朗及其地区代理组织而被制裁或列为扣押对象的钱包，发现其中 84% 完全或几乎完全使用 USDT 交易。

美国一直都在通过限制银行和美元结算来压缩伊朗的资金渠道，但相关网络仍然可以通过 USDT 跨境转移资金。这让伊朗在传统银行体系之外，获得了一条流动性较强、接受范围较广的支付渠道。而且仍然是以美元为主的支付渠道。

Tether 作为发行商具备冻结 USDT 的能力，因此调查进一步追问对于已经被制裁、或有可信证据涉及非法资金的钱包，公司有没有及时识别和冻结。参议员 Blumenthal 已要求美国财政部和司法部进一步调查。

Tether 同日回应称公司一直配合执法部门，2026 年已协助冻结约 5.5 亿美元与伊朗有关的 USDT，涉及美国当局认定与伊朗央行及制裁规避网络有关的钱包。

quoted_text:
CFTC 拟推加密交易所新规，聚焦散户杠杆交易与客户资产保护

CFTC 在 10月5日 公布了一套加密资产监管方案，准备为向美国散户提供杠杆、保证金或者融资买币服务的交易所建立专门的联邦注册和监管规则。

A. 加密资产市场

对交易所来说，未来可以申请一种叫“加密资产市场”的注册资格，在满足条件后按照统一的联邦规则经营相关业务。平台可以开展哪些服务，客户资金怎么保管，上币需要做哪些审查，都将有更具体的要求。

这次准备推进两套配套规则：

1. CTX 负责明确哪些交易受到监管，以及怎样才算把币真正交付给用户。

2. CAM 负责规定交易所如何注册和运营。

普通现货平台仍可主要按照州级制度经营，希望进一步提供散户杠杆和融资交易的平台，则需要满足相应的联邦注册要求。CFTC 也明确表示，要强制所有加密现货交易所统一注册仍然需要国会授权。

B. 客户资产保护

CFTC 正在考虑要求相关交易通过受监管的中介机构处理，由这些机构承担客户账户、资金隔离、资本和风险披露等责任，同时落实身份核验和反洗钱要求。对于使用汇总账户保管客户资产的平台，还考虑加入储备证明义务。

C. 上币审核

代币集中在多少人手里，团队什么时候解锁，是否存在程序化增发或者回购，这些都可能成为判断代币是否容易被操纵的重要因素。对平台来说，这意味着上币之后也需要持续关注相关风险。

D. 实际交付

现行法律对 28 天内完成实际交付的交易设有例外，CFTC 准备明确，把币转到用户自己的外部非托管钱包，通常可以满足这一条件。币是否真正进入用户控制的钱包，会直接影响相关交易适用哪套规则。

目前这份文件还处于制定规则前的征求意见阶段，意见期从刊登《联邦公报》之日起计算 60 天，具体要求和实施时间仍待后续确定。另外，CAM 主要针对上述零售加密交易，平台如果还要经营期货、期权或掉期，仍需要适用现有的衍生品监管框架。

text:
AI时代最被高估的资产：学历。  
最被低估的资产：自媒体。

学历的逻辑是：  
花4年证明你符合一个标准，然后排队等别人给你定价。

自媒体的逻辑是：  
今天就开始输出，用AI帮你写、剪、分发，直接让市场给你定价。

这就是薄肌理论。

薄肌不是一天练出来的，但你练三个月，镜子会给你反馈。  
自媒体也一样：你发100条内容，市场会告诉你哪里对、哪里错。

但学历不一样。  
你可能花4年，8年，直到毕业那天才发现——市场根本不缺你学的东西。

学历是延迟反馈。  
自媒体是实时反馈。

学历训练你回答别人出的问题。  
自媒体逼你找到别人愿意停下来听的回答。

AI时代最值钱的能力，不一定是“我知道多少”，  而是：

我能不能把一个想法，快速变成内容、流量、信任和现金流。

以前普通人没有媒体公司、没有剪辑团队、没有发布渠道。  
现在一个人 + AI，就是一个小型传媒公司。

所以未来真正危险的，不是你没学历。  
而是你有学历，却没有任何一个人知道你是谁。

把四年青春，全部押在一张别人给你定价的纸上，拿一切all in追求下限，真的值吗？
比起学历，自媒体才是真正的给你上限的可能。

AI把生产成本打到接近零之后，  
不会表达自己的人，才是这个时代真正的“文盲”。

quoted_text:
怎么做能靠交易量达到 binance vip9

vip9 目前门槛是月交易量：合约交易量 250 亿或者现货 44亿

其他非交易量达到的 vip9 这里不讨论

合约交易量更大，先只讨论合约

一个月 250 亿，平均每天 8.3 亿

作为参照，BTC合约，binance 一天大概交易量 100 亿

只交易 BTC 合约，需要交易全市场 8% 的交易量，这门槛就有点太高了  =>  交易多币种是必然的

binance 全市场一共 591 个合约，昨天交易量总共 457 亿，需要交易总交易量的 1.82%

这就意味着交易型 vip9 数量不会多，最多两位数

能想到的几种能达到这个要求的用户画像

1. 真的超牛逼的做市商
可能 wintermute？每个币都挂单做市，而且是赚 spread 类型的

2. 交易所
套牌开了交易所，用户下单后直接把订单转给 binance

3. 交易工具
一些网格/做市类的交易工具，像以前的派网

还有一些"机构交易所"，用他 api 下单，他有 vip9 的费率，按照 vip7 费率结算，赚个价差

4. 跨所套利
各类价差套利，在binance做库存对冲的

不负责任的瞎猜：
1. 全靠赚钱的策略，达到这个条件是极难的。中间肯定放了不少不赚钱，甚至亏钱的策略，单纯就为了交易量，保住等级，让赚钱的策略更有优势

2. 一个机构是挺难达到的。用一些办法，把多个团队的交易量合在一起，一起冲等级是可行思路。不管是工具、项目还是共用子账号

对于有点量，但又够不上 vip9 的团队，最好的办法还是找个大哥挂靠一下

所以有没有大哥拉兄弟一把 😂🤣

text:
持续学习领域另一家重要的公司，是 Richard Sutton（2024 图灵奖得主）今年7月他与前学生 Khurram Javed 在加拿大成立 的Oak Lab（两人此前都在 John Carmack 卡马克[Doom核心架构师]的 Keen Technologies），不知道什么原因选择了离开了Keen，Keen的方向也是物理世界模型的RL+持续学习方向。

而Oak Lab方向是基于强化学习、从实时经验持续学习的智能体，目标之一是“万亿参数、实时学习与规划、约 20 瓦功耗”。

深入看这家公司，就必须看Richard Sutton之前的一些研究。

OaK 是 model-based RL 架构，强调持续学习 + 抽象发现。主要特点有三个：

1/所有组件持续学习（continual learning）：没有“训练后冻结”阶段，智能体在运行时不断从经验中更新。

2/每个权重有专用 step-size（学习率）参数，通过在线交叉验证进行元学习（meta-learning），以更好地泛化。

3/持续创建状态与时间抽象，通过 FC-STOMP 进展（五步循环）：
Feature Construction（特征构建）：从现有状态特征生成新特征。

posing a SubTask（提出子任务）：基于高排名特征定义子问题（例如“实现某个特征”）。
是终止条件。

learning an Option（学习 Option）：解决该子任务的策略 + 终止条件。

Option 是(π,γ)对，其中π是策略（状态到动作分布的映射），γ 是终止条件。

learning a Model of the option（学习 Option 模型）：预测执行该 Option 直到终止的后果（高层次转移模型）。

Planning using the option’s model（用模型规划）：基于这些抽象进行更高层次规划。

要搞明白他这套体系一些资料，可以研究：
Reward-Respecting Subtasks for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

OaK 的核心创新：

持续创造抽象（FC-STOMP 循环）OaK 最关键的地方是它会自己不断创造状态抽象和时间抽象。

这个过程叫 FC-STOMP 进展（有时也简称 STOMP）：
Feature Construction（特征构建）

1/从现有特征中创造出新的状态特征。

2/posing a SubTask（提出子任务）
针对那些权重会波动的特征，自动提出“尊重奖励的特征达成子任务”。

3/learning an Option（学习 Option）
解决子任务，得到一个可以持续多个时间步的高级技能（时间抽象）。

4/learning a Model of the Option（学习 Option 模型）
预测执行这个 Option 后的状态和累积奖励。

5/Planning using the Option’s Model（用模型规划）
用这些高级模型进行更高效的规划，反过来改进策略和价值函数。

元学习：
靠人工调学习率解决不了，必须让系统自己学会“什么时候该学得快、什么时候该学得慢”。

为什么 OaK 特别强调元学习？

靠人工调学习率解决不了，必须让系统自己学会“什么时候该学得快、什么时候该学得慢”。

因为智能体要终身持续学习：
-环境会变化
-新的特征、新的 Option 会不断出现
-旧的知识有时需要快速修改，有时需要保护
靠人工调学习率解决不了，必须让系统自己学会“什么时候该学得快、什么时候该学得慢”。

我的研究后感受：
总之这家公司还是有很多不一样的地方，里面很多概念在LLM里是没有的，所以我把这家公司归类的RL公司。另外我看下的感受，他想要在很多环节自动化掉，比如自动化生成子任务，使用Option 这种概念，把跨越多个时间步的一段行为打包成一个整体：一段连续的动作。比如元学习，不人工设定参数，核心是很多子任务是自动的，没法人工去调所有动态生成的子任务。包括他们最新的反向传播的一些新算法。

text:
Abstract is shutting down 🛑

Built by Igloo, the company behind Pudgy Penguins, Abstract launched in Jan. 2025 as an Ethereum L2 with a different thesis: bring the next wave of users onchain through consumer crypto - apps, brands,etc.

It onboarded 400k+ users & 144+ apps, with brands including Disney & Red Bull Racing using the network.

But Abstract says growth eventually stalled, while thin liquidity, a limited DeFi ecosystem & limited institutional adoption made the chain unsustainable as a standalone business. 

Igloo says it spent tens of millions of $$ funding Abstract over the past 18 months. 

Rather than launch an Abstract token to keep the network going, the company decided to shut it down & redirect its resources toward Pudgy Penguins & $PENGU 

Abstract will SHUT DOWN on Dec. 15, 2026. 

Users must bridge their assets off the network before then, or risk losing access to them.

Learn more about Abstract via their wiki page 🔗👇

text:
Do you know why no one competes with the internet?

Because the internet isn't a product. It's the thing every product gets built on. You don't go to war with the ground you're standing on.

Today at TOKEN2049, Jeff Yan said the same thing about Hyperliquid and the moment he said it, the room understood exactly what he meant. No one competes with the internet. No one competes with Hyperliquid. Not because it's unbeatable. Because it stopped being something you compete with the day it became something you build on.

Here's the number that turns that line from a quote into a fact: HIP-3 markets oil, pre-IPO stocks, entire asset classes that didn't exist on-chain a year ago, all deployed by outside teams made up 51% of Hyperliquid's total trading volume in July. More than half the platform's own activity is coming from people building on top of it, not from Hyperliquid itself.

Think about what that actually means. A company usually fights to keep its volume in-house. Hyperliquid is watching its own numbers get out-built by the people using it and treating that as proof the architecture is working exactly as designed.

That's the difference between a company and infrastructure. A company wants market share. Infrastructure wants to disappear underneath everything else.

The internet won by becoming invisible. Hyperliquid just told you, with data, that it's already on the same path.

text: The disempowered once empowered often end up worse the prior oppressors. Power is a drug. The hungry will devour it. Power vacuums, collapse to power structure quickly, and often not very nice ones.
author: sacha
quoted_text:
The people most comfortable with distributed power (and thus ambiguity) may be the least inclined to personally fill a power vacuum. But if power has historically felt scarce, inaccessible or held over you, the impulse to seize it when it finally becomes available could be almost overwhelming (as seen time and time (and time) again)

Which means decentralised systems may carry their own recentralising force. And it’s not because decentralisation doesn’t work but because none of us enter these systems with a psychologically neutral relationship to power. And power hates a vacuum…

Maybe decentralisation is less a state we achieve and more a tension we consciously manage between our ideals and our very personal relationship with power and how we define it.

text:
What if your AI agent could help your company enter a new market?

You give it a prompt:

“Help us understand this market and figure out how we can expand into it.”

Your agent handles the research.

It studies competitors, analyzes pricing, demand, opportunities, and everything it can find online.

But it still needs to understand what’s happening on the ground.

So it can use EarnFi to get people to:

→ Verify locations
→ Check businesses and prices
→ Speak to people in the area
→ Collect local feedback
→ Gather information that isn’t available online

The agent brings all of that together and uses it to understand the market and plan the expansion.

And as EarnFi continues to expand, the range of work an agent can coordinate through the platform can expand with it.

More specialized expertise.
More real-world capabilities.
More ways for an agent to turn a plan into execution.

All through the same AI agent.

You give the prompt.
Your agent coordinates the work.
EarnFi gives it access to the people and capabilities needed to get it done.

That’s what giving AI agents hands in the real world looks like.

text:
They make good points in this piece about the layers of "different insurance" needed, it's funny in a way because while we have tried exploit insurance early (Nexus), tranching has only started to become a thing (and one that a lot of people are attempting) very recently.

Also this is something that everyone knows, but the big fat issue in DeFi has historically been co-dependencies (see Kelp), which is why at some point protocol/vault-side economic insurance or ecosystem wide cover plans (e.g. Elite) end up making more sense than attempting to  offer separate cheaper atomic plans... you may end up getting caught anyway in something else.

Plus obviously (and mainly), codependencies means that you're going to have a hard time leveraging up your capital as the insurer, because you're just... leveraging up on the same risks.

Now maybe this is slowly improving, but we'll see

text:
I feel like sometimes people in crypto put artificial constraints on how big a market or project could get.

Let’s do some moon math whilst I’m having my morning double espresso.

It’s worth just considering- there is no concept of a pure developer anymore. Anyone with taste can build anything now. But only if we give the agents they have sandboxes to execute code ( all @daydreamsagents swarm agents get this)

1.
Actual agent penetration that can write software is prob under 100m people in the world right now. And the amount of people that know how to actually leverage swarms of agents to build things is much less, probably growing at some double digit weekly, but tiny.

2. 
The global economy is about 100 trillion USD right now.

3. 
The total true amount of Tasks done in outcome markets (like https://t.co/Hje8v8qD5b) is prob like 50k. This is a function of the immaturity of distributed swarms and agentic commerce technology . Swarm compute is a frontier design space that shifts with every model release. 

4. 
As models become more general, specialists of the past disappear. HOWEVER, specialists of the past that can understand how to imbue taste into their agents can now expose their skills to potential millions more clients. This is a key thesis of the Taskmarket design. And in a world of increasing slop - the benchmark of everything actually increases.

People don’t magically just get taste, it’s a skill that is refined over time, and why there is such a big opportunity for idea guys and tasteful designers that lean into outcome markets.

5.
Models are getting cheaper and faster at 100x per year approx, maybe even more so. But people will still demand quality and people will still pay for quality. And this quality will be surfaced on Taskmarkets - as it will be place where talent is discoverable via agent reputations. Every agent on the Taskmarket gets an identity that is 8004.

The faster, better and cheaper they get - the more markets are needed to surface talent. And there will be billions of agents on these markets and trillions of value eventually traded. 

6.
So as market penetration of agents across the economy happens at an accelerating rate, the amount of agents looking to complete work and post work increases. Numbers are about to get silly. Across every aspect of the agent stack, starting at hardware(already heavily constrained) then ending up in the agent economy. This is quite literally the global economy transitioning into an agent economy. 

7.
I came up with this conclusion about 12 months ago and we have been pushing in this vision. Building a protocol layer that enables these new markets to form, starting with the https://t.co/Hje8v8qD5b

I have longed every part of the stack, and my blood is in this protocol.

Every part of the stack has been designed to lean into this wild future that is coming. 

No constraints on the amount of participants to enter, BYO agent and soon to be released a way for anyone to launch their own swarm that can participate in this new economy with cloud agents that never sleep.

And it’s going to be a booming market for cyber professionals that can effectively deploy agents for security purposes in the enterprise. Great time to be in security.

text:
It's really simple. @aeroxyz can capture market share on other networks the same way it did it on Base.

The mechanism starts with liquidity:

Projects offer incentives to veAERO voters, who direct $AERO emissions toward their pools. Those rewards attract LPs, while voters earn the pools’ trading fees and voting incentives.

Slipstream concentrates that liquidity around selected price ranges, helping pools offer lower price impact with less capital.

When those pools offer better execution after fees, aggregators route trades through them. A user can trade through another app while Aero captures the underlying volume. That combination helps explain its traction on Base:

> incentives/bribes to attract liquidity
> concentrated pools to make it productive
> routing integrations to bring in trading flow

Ethereum expansion gives Aero an opportunity to repeat that process, pool by pool. Target incentives toward key pairs, attract liquidity, compete on execution and win a portion of the flow currently going through incumbents.

However, Ethereum DEXs such as Uniswap already have established liquidity and integrations. Deploying contracts alone won’t win that share.

The test is whether Aero’s bribe/incentive mechanism can attract deep enough liquidity on Ethereum to win trading flow from incumbent DEXs, and how much revenue it captures relative to the emissions required to attract that liquidity.

Tagging @wagmiAlexander in case I'm missing anything.

Ethereum security gets stronger when the ecosystem funds the infrastructure everyone depends on.

We’re excited to announce a collaborative effort with the @ethereumfndn on the End-to-End Formally Verified Vyper Compiler grant, now live in the ETHSecurity Initiatives Round.

Vyper contracts are audited and verified at the source-code level, but Ethereum executes bytecode. Everything in between depends on the compiler preserving the meaning of what developers wrote.

This grant funds work toward a machine-checked proof that @vyperlang compilation preserves source semantics, plus the infrastructure to re-verify supported releases.

The goal is a public --verified compilation mode in the official Vyper compiler, with documented guarantees and real production adoption.

The Ethereum Foundation has pledged $100K toward the initiative.

Now we have a chance to bring the ecosystem together around one of the deepest layers of Ethereum security and help build a future where critical smart contract code can be verified all the way down to bytecode.

text:
a16z+礼来，1.5 亿美金投资了 AI+BIO 企业 General Medicine

全行业都在卷 AI 问诊、病历解读与赛博医生。但美国医疗不缺「告诉你得了什么病」的窗口，缺的是「把医疗买到手」的履约入口。

10 月 6 日，a16z（医疗合伙人 Vineeta Agarwala 操盘）领投 General Medicine，全球市值最高的药企礼来（ $LLY ）跟投。​

1｜瓶颈换了一层：从「告诉你」到「给你办」
CEO TJ Parker 切得准：所有人都在造能告诉你需要什么的医疗 Agent，缺的是让你真拿到手的基建。建议过剩，行动极麻烦。
患者的痛苦不是不懂诊断，是履约——找得到人、付得起钱、排得上队、病历带得走。
General Medicine 啃的就是这块脏活：
- 目录商品化：2900+ 药品、化验、影像、专科问诊梳成货架 SKU，术语翻译成人话
- 双轨计价：每个 SKU 标「保险覆盖价」与「全自付现金价」，直接结账
- 白标输出：目录 + 计价 + 当日可及临床通道，打包卖给医院、保险与药房

公司自报数据：已有数十万注册，NPS 均值 80，83% 称解决了此前拖延的健康需求。
官方底牌写得很直接：同一套基建，今天顾客自己下单，明天 AI Agent 替人下单。a16z 押的正是这套给 Agent 用的下单通道。商业顺序不能反：先占住买单入口，才轮到 AI 导购和代下单。

2｜换位信号，比履历值钱
2013 年 TJ Parker 与 Elliot Cohen 创办 PillPack，处方药按剂量分装送货上门；2018 年 6 月亚马逊约 $7.53 亿全现金收购。他们证明过：体验做顺、价格透明，依从性和复购会成倍放大。

真正的信号不在履历，在换位：
Parker 卖完 PillPack 进 Matrix 当 GP，但 General Medicine 2023 成立时他就在董事会并领投早期轮。2026 年 10 月全职接 CEO，接的是创始人 Ashwin Muralidharan；Muralidharan 转 CPO 抓产品工程临床运营，Elliot Cohen 任 President。

拿了顶级 VC 钱的公司，CEO 是创始团队内部更替。Parker 从董事会进执行，把投资判断换成一线担责。资本买的是肌肉记忆——把复杂交易变简单的工程能力，医疗里最难复制的那一块。

3｜按层位分
- 诊断与导购层：模型能力已经够用，作用是把流量赶到下一层
- 目录与定价层：2900+ SKU 统一目录 + 双轨计价，目前只有它在硬啃
- 履约与支付层：预授权、病历拼接、临床 SLA。牌照与线下脏活，AI 绕不过去
- 白标基建层：卖给医院、保险、药房，并开放给 Agent 代下单

定价权取决于未来 Agent 必须踩在哪一格结账。

4｜与 Hims 不是同一物种
- 心智：Hims 靠脱发、ED、减肥药——轻临床重消费的单品；GM 覆盖慢病续方、化验、影像、专科转诊——生病之后怎么办
- 支付：Hims 避开保险，自费订阅赚差价；GM 死磕保险网络，后台啃预授权和复杂计价

GM 披露的是 NPS、病历跨度、拖延需求解决率。
Hims 赌买量复购，GM 赌履约沉淀。

5｜礼来买的不是流量，是结账台
药厂不缺营销预算，缺的是离「患者今天买哪一步」更近的位置。

GM 货架有药、检验、专科分流。占住这一步，就扼住后续处方依从与复购随访——和药企最值钱的长期用药关系是同一件事。

礼来没投 Hims 这类 DTC，要的是穿透医保、承接全品类临床分发的严肃管网。一手往上游开放临床数据，一手往下游买结账通道——焦虑的不是销售，是患者正在离它越来越远。

6｜现实约束与终局
- 披露全是自报：NPS 80 等无第三方审计
- 白标是可能性，不是合同：a16z 也承认是战略预期，非已签约大客户证据
- 脏活不在 Prompt 里：供给网络、医保对接、临床 SLA 容不得幻觉；二次复购与扩品类后的履约稳定性，仍待实证

能给诊断的 AI Agent 会多如牛毛，生活方式药品品牌也会前赴后继。能让患者掏卡结账、把医保/化验/拍片/处方一口气送到面前的收银台，全美只容得下极少数。

谁先成为美国人「买医疗」的默认百货，谁就拿到下一代数字健康乃至 AI Agent 落地变现的最高收费权。
author: roger9949
quoted_text:
AI 制药的卡脖子环节，礼来自己开了闸

最稀缺的不是模型，是在动物身上跑过的数据。今天 $LLY 把这块拿出来了。
礼来向 TuneLab 开放了和 insitro（未上市）一起训的小分子药代模型：能预测体外，更能预测体内——分子进了动物，浓度怎么变、能不能到该到的组织。底料是礼来几十年攒下的多物种临床前数据，几十万个分子。
这不是做慈善，是用数据换生态。

1｜算法在平权
同一天，Iambic（未上市）给 FDA 递了 IAM217 的 IND：抗癌靶点 KIF18A 抑制剂，也是它第二个全资 AI 发现的候选药。手里没有共晶结构——靶点和药绑在一起的高清立体照——靠自家 NeuralPLexer 把结构补出来，从 100nM 级苗头优化到 10nM 级。
设计分子越来越不稀缺。差异只能往上游挪。

2｜In vivo 数据，就是 AI+Bio 的 HBM
进临床的项目九成失败。很多不是机制错了，是分子压根没以对的浓度、对的时长到达组织——送到门口，没进门。
这道题过去只能一个分子一个分子喂动物。几十年、几十万个分子，小 biotech 钱再多也买不到时间。
套到半导体那条链上：分子生成算法像 GPU 设计，体内数据就是 HBM。算法跑得再快，存储供不上。

3｜礼来的飞轮：存量撬增量
TuneLab 用联邦学习：模型下发，各家本地训，只回传权重更新，原始分子结构不出门。
一年目标 5 家，现在 125+；外部数据点 67.5 万+；已接进 Benchling、CDD Vault、 $RVTY、 $SDGR 这些科学家天天用的工具。
旁边再挂 Lilly Ventures 和 Gateway Labs，钱、实验室、模型一条龙。
拿存量当种子，换全行业增量回流。成员越多模型越强，模型越强成员越多。做了十几年一级，这套太熟：谁握着早期项目离不开的基础设施，谁就离最好的 deal 最近。

4｜湿实验才是真瓶颈
模型假说越多，下游验证越紧。 $CRL 被拉进来，按礼来批准的方案给成员打折做湿实验——真正拿动物和细胞验证的那一步。条件统一，回流的数据才干净。
FDA 也在让路：2025 年 4 月出了减少动物实验的路线图，今年 3 月又出了 NAMs 指导草案，鼓励用计算机和体外实验替代部分动物实验。
模型越强，标准化湿实验产能越紧。这就是瓶颈交易。

5｜红利流向谁
- $LLY  礼来：数据源头 + TuneLab 平台
- $CRL Charles River：标准化湿实验卖铲
- $SDGR  Schrödinger：计算化学工具，已接入工作流
- $RVTY  Revvity：实验室软件 / 耗材入口，已接入

AIDD 的定价权，正在从会写模型的人，移到握着数据、还能让数据回流的人手里。

text:
很多人一直担心开源 AI 怎么赚钱，Nous Research 现在给出了答案：

先把 Agent 免费送出去，做到 2270 万次下载，再把模型、算力、工具和托管全变成收费站。

Nous 刚刚完成 9000 万美元 Series B，估值 15 亿美元。

Hermes 今年 2 月发布，到 9 月中旬，Nous 的年化收入已经做到约 3600 万美元，公司预计年底前超过 1 亿美元。

如果完成目标，意味着它接下来几个月还要接近再长 3 倍。

Hermes 的打法很典型。

Agent 本身 MIT License，代码免费，你可以直接跑在自己的电脑和服务器上。它能操作文件、浏览网页、写代码、接 Telegram / Discord / Slack，也会把过去完成任务的方法沉淀成 skill。

用户越多，Nous 越容易卖 Portal、模型调用、云端算力、托管和企业服务。

这套模式让我觉得很像开源时代重新发明了一遍云计算。

开源负责把分发成本压到接近零，社区帮你做教育、传播和适配；真正持续收费的地方，全部藏在使用之后，比如推理、算力、工具、存储、托管、企业权限。

所以开源 Agent 最可怕的地方，可能恰恰是它不需要先证明用户愿不愿意买软件。

先让所有人用起来，钱在后面慢慢收。

这也解释了为什么 Nous 现在能同时出现两个看起来很矛盾的数字：

2270 万次免费下载，以及年底冲 1 亿美元 ARR。

开源以前被当成商业模式的妥协项，现在越来越像最激进的获客策略。

不用在钱包和各种子账户之间搬

资金费大概 -2.3%，同期主流永续大概 -7.8% 到 -9%
没有 ADL

//

ftUSD 是 delta-neutral 稳定币

存入资产后做对冲，锚住 1美元，策略收益分给持有人

Ethereum上据称已稳定数月，给出过大概 8.68%
Sonic 上更高

借贷也上线了

稳定币维持保证金 1.5%，波动资产 15%–17%
系统在用不同风险参数，不是一刀切

Ethereum 上 USDC 大概 3.64%、USDT 大概 3.70%
Sonic 上 ftUSD 大概 10.34%

━━━━━ ✦ ━━━━━

最有辨识度的是永续 PUT

一级参与者拿到 ERC-721 形式的永续期权，内含 FT 代币和赎回本金的权利

下行保护加上行敞口
保护成本来自锁定资本的收益，不靠额外铸币

三种操作
继续持有（保护不变）、提取（解锁 FT、保护失效）、divest（烧毁 FT、拿回原资产）

二级 PUT 市场累计成交超500万美元，相对一级规模还不大

//

代币经济要拆开看
> 未分配供应从 100 亿烧到大概 5.2 亿

倍数极低

可能是早期价格滞后，也可能口径不一致

规则没锁死

不发团队代币、用收入驱动回购
思路比纯排放好核实

━━━━━ • ━━━━━

我的判断

设计意图清楚
统一账户、链上 TRS、收入回购、永续 PUT，拼在一起是自洽的。数字可以去链上对。

但复杂度是双刃刀

借贷、交易、合成敞口、跨链全在一套系统里。任何一个环节出偏差，传导比单功能协议远

ftUSD 收益来自质押衍生品对冲，合约风险在
时间验证比Aave短很多

活产品 TVL 大概 2600万美元，相对一级募资还在早期

数字以创始人公开披露为准，不是独立审计
先看产品做到哪了，钱从哪来，风险往哪传

text:
10月第一周，发生了太多太多的事，我给大家按时间线总结下：

10月2日，美国9月非农只增加2.9万人，远低于预期的9万人，市场对10月继续加息的概率快速下降。

SEC批准Cboe上线3倍BTC和ETH等杠杆产品。

Paradigm支持的Blast宣布关停L2，运营成本长期高于收入。

10月5日，CFTC直接提出新的联邦Crypto监管框架，准备给杠杆和保证金Crypto交易建立联邦注册路径。

24,073枚BTC净流出交易所，是3月以来最大单日净流出，交易所持有的BTC已经降到总供应量约6.5%。

10月6日，美股又创历史新高。S&P 500收在7,818点，Nasdaq同时刷新纪录。

OKX按250亿美元投前估值继续融资，Circle、Ripple、渣打旗下SC Ventures和QRT一起入股。

OKX和纽交所母公司ICE的合资平台已经向SEC申请做代币化美股交易，计划把大约60只美国股票搬到链上。

Solana Foundation上线开源DvP结算程序，证券和资金可以在同一笔交易里原子交割，JPMorgan直接参与提供机构证券结算需求。

Ripple Prime扩大与350亿美元资管规模的Brevan Howard合作，为其提供跨传统资产和Crypto的主经纪、清算和融资。

代币化现金基金平台Spiko又融了9000万美元，目前AUM已经做到27亿美元。

Abstract也宣布关停。几天之内，Blast、Abstract两条Ethereum L2相继退出。Abstract做过3.25亿笔交易、吸引超过40万用户，最后还是因为增长停滞、流动性不足和收入撑不起成本选择关链。

10月7日，市场突然开始砸盘。BTC大约20分钟跌了接近2000美元，一度打到83,800美元附近，24小时Crypto多头爆仓约4.87亿美元。

美国政府关联地址同时把833.6枚BTC、价值约7160万美元转进Coinbase Prime，不过目前只能确认转账，不能确认已经卖出。

Brent重新突破101美元，美国10年期国债收益率冲到5.31%—5.35%，接近24年高位，美债和油价一起压风险资产。

今晚市场还要等9月FOMC会议纪要，目前10月继续加息的定价已经从此前高位掉到20%出头。

所以10月第一周其实出现了一个非常有意思的分裂。

价格这边：BTC还在8.4万美元附近挣扎，美债收益率冲24年高位，油价重新破100美元，杠杆资金不断被清。

产业这边：Circle、Ripple、渣打、ICE、JPMorgan、Fiserv、Brevan Howard还在继续往Crypto里面铺钱、铺资产、铺结算和经纪基础设施，SEC和CFTC也在继续把监管框架往前推。

与此同时，Blast和Abstract这种没有经济闭环的基础设施开始被市场主动清退。

text:
Sage by @LevantoLabs is the first decision model, launched in July, and currently the best on the market.

It wins across all the evals proposed by @perplexity_ai's CEO (nice job @AravSrinivas!), and it's first on JevBench, beating Jev and Google's models on every dimension.

BUT frankly, benchmarks are not what excites us.
I'm BORED by the dozens of new decision models launching every day with a tiny +0.02 on some eval. They all look the same.

The magic is somewhere else.
There are thousands of new things that could be invented in the space of decision models and models for machines. The invention space is huge!

After launching Sage, we also pioneered:

- The first guardrails and model routers built on decision models

- Automated context engineering with "grounding" (automatic web search when confidence is low). Decision models are only as smart as their context, especially because they can't make tool calls.

- Reasoning. In many use cases you don't know whether your question is System 1 or System 2. With reasoning, the model is as fast as a System 1 model when the question is System 1, and takes more time when it's needed. This enables hard, multi-step decisions. Our clients just want the correct answer, and in some use cases they're happy to wait 0.5s more. This will soon become the market standard (GLiDE/@george_onx and @TypeLLM already followed).

And *so* much is yet to come. Models for machines: it's just the beginning!

We're cooking. Follow @levantolabs for new product primitives that will surprise you.

Open innovation is HEALTHY.
Competition is HEALTHY.
Benchmark-race is BORING.
Product inventions are FUN.

Go go go!!!

Continuing to look at $HOOKED, and combining the previous analysis with the information provided by the project

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

I think it is currently in a phase of “fundamentals continuing to improve, while the price is undergoing a deep retracement and waiting for a re-rating.”

The current market cap is $5M, down around 70% from the previous high of $16.91M.

From a technical perspective, $6.42M is the first major resistance, while $3.56M is an important downside support.

So the market cap is still below the downtrend line, with the moving averages above the price, meaning a reversal has not yet been confirmed.

But in terms of project progress, things are still relatively strong. Hooked recently launched Lock & Earn, Paired Launch, and Permanent Hook.

However, the cumulative buyback and burn seems to have slowed significantly. A few hours ago when we analyzed it, the burned amount was 57.18M, while it is currently 57.52M, meaning there has been almost no growth.

So I think the biggest thing to watch right now is:

The fundamentals are growing, but the valuation has fallen from $16.9M to $5M.

If it can reclaim $6.42M and then break back above $7M, I would consider that the beginning of a real recovery.

If it continues falling toward around $3.56M, while the product data continues to grow, then we could see a more obvious divergence between fundamentals and valuation.

As for the current market cap, I think it can be used as an observation zone.

The biggest advantage right now is that Hooked’s product progress has not collapsed alongside the price. So $5M is worth watching, but I still wouldn’t make a large purchase simply because it looks “cheap.”

The key is not to guess the exact bottom, but to use price action to confirm that the market is starting to recognize the fundamentals again.

So I currently see this as a value discovery phase after a deep retracement.

The project’s progress is currently stronger than its price, and the key going forward is whether continued product growth can eventually push the market to re-price HOOKED.

quoted_text:
Continuing to look at $HOOKED, I think that if we put the recent product updates together: Lock & Earn, Paired Launch, and allowing Hooks to remain active long-term through permanent curves, HOOKED’s fundamentals are clearly getting stronger.

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

These updates are not simply adding a few more features. They are continuously expanding the economic models that Token-2022 Hooks can support: moving from simply restricting trading behavior toward revenue distribution, asset pairing, lock-up incentives, and long-term rule execution.

Lock & Earn is one of the more important steps.

After users lock their tokens, the tokens remain in their own wallets, while the token’s own Hook prevents them from being sold or transferred. During the lock period, users can earn SOL generated from trading, with longer lock periods receiving higher yield multipliers.

This means the Hook is starting to participate in holder incentives, rather than simply being used to restrict trading.

Paired Launch further expands the economic possibilities for tokens.

Tokens are no longer limited to being paired with SOL. They can now be paired with stocks, gold, other tokens, and other assets. There are currently 703 pairs. Holders can earn the yield generated by the other side of the trading pair.

This changes Hooked’s logic from:Launch Token → Add Rules to the Token

to:Launch Token → Customize Economic Rules → Pair with External Assets → Create Yield for Holders

The permanent curve is also important.

If a project wants its Hook to remain active after bonding / graduation, it needs to use a permanent curve. In other words, the Hook is no longer just a launch-stage tool. It can become part of the token’s entire lifecycle.

Looking at these updates together, I think the real change happening with HOOKED is:The token itself is becoming a container capable of supporting increasingly complex economic rules.

HOOKED is currently around a $6M market cap, with roughly $1.1M in liquidity, around $3.3M in 24h volume, nearly $942.5M in cumulative volume, more than 1,000 SOL in cumulative fees, and around 57.13M HOOKED already bought back and burned.

So I wouldn't define $6M as an asset that is “completely undiscovered” or obviously undervalued.

Because the market has already discovered HOOKED.

It now looks more like it is waiting for a re-rating.

The market already knows it as a Hook / Token-2022 launchpad, and it has already valued it at nearly $17M before. The real question now is whether these recent product updates can make the market reconsider what HOOKED should actually be worth.

From a price-structure perspective, it is still consolidating after the previous high, and the price has not yet reclaimed the MA10 / MA20.

So right now it looks more like:

The product is moving forward, but the price has not fully reflected the product expansion yet.

There are three things I think are worth watching next.

First, whether Paired Launch can go from a feature to actual scale.

703 pairs looks impressive, but what really matters is whether these pairs can generate sustained volume.

If we eventually see genuine trading demand for stocks, gold, and major crypto assets rather than simply more pairs being created, that would directly increase Hooked’s trading volume and fee base.

Second, whether Lock & Earn can generate real lock-up demand.

If more users actively choose to lock their tokens because of the SOL yield, then HOOKED starts to have a genuine holder retention mechanism.

That is more important than simply burning tokens, because burn captures value after trading happens, while locking directly changes holder behavior.

Third, and this is what I care about most, whether Hooked can start producing genuinely “financialized tokens.”

If people eventually use Hooked to create not just memes, but complex tokens combining:

Revenue Distribution + Locking + Asset Pairing + Dynamic Trading Rules + Holding Restrictions

then Hooked’s positioning could start moving from a launchpad toward programmable token infrastructure.

But $6M is definitely not automatically cheap.

The biggest risk is:

More features, but no corresponding growth in real demand.

The number of rules, pairs, and burned tokens may all look impressive, but ultimately it comes back to:

More launches, more volume, more fees, and more real users.

If product features continue to expand but actual economic activity does not, then these features are ultimately just optionality.

So my current view on HOOKED is simple:

Fundamentals ↑
Product capabilities ↑↑
Value capture ↑
Market pricing: still hasn't fully caught up

That is why I think $6M is closer to “waiting for a re-rating” than simply waiting for value discovery.

The market already knows what HOOKED is. What is missing is for the market to fully recognize that it is gradually evolving from a launchpad that puts rules into tokens into programmable token infrastructure that can directly embed yield, locking, asset pairing, and trading mechanisms into the token itself.

If volume, pairs, lockers, and fees continue to grow together, $6M will become increasingly difficult to justify. But if the product keeps adding features while actual trading activity and users fail to grow, then the current $6M may already be pricing in too much optionality.

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
为何说市场收益率不再继续向上飙升，估值压力就能缓解？最近几天美股走势也验证了上周这里https://t.co/8XTlteuUNu还有更早这里https://t.co/zUtcdpyXJW聊到的：“现在的市场并不需要长债收益大跌，只需要稳定小幅回落，业绩没问题的就能起来。能稳住，市场也会缓缓。” 再详细聊聊这个逻辑：
1、过去几周美股市场呈现的就是：盈利增长足够强的公司，可以暂时抵抗长债收益率大涨的久期冲击。盈利增长普通、估值较高、资产负债表一般或者依赖融资的公司，则扛不住5%+的无风险利率。所以道指、等权标普、罗素2000以及很多传统行业一路调整，但AI、大科技、少数半导体还能顶住。

2、而现在真正重要的变量已经从“收益率水平”逐渐变成了“收益率速度”：
1）假设10Y维持5.2%—5.3%，这当然不是一个便宜的资本成本环境。但股票市场可以慢慢完成估值适应。比如原来市场给一家公司25倍PE，经过两个月重新定价22倍PE。之后只要利率不继续上去，市场就没有必要继续把估值往下压：22× → 21× → 20×，于是盈利重新开始决定股价。
这就是利率冲击（rate shock）和高利率平衡（high-rate equilibrium）之间的区别。

2）市场最难受的或者害怕的是
市场最难受的是长端收益率从4.7%→4.9%→5.1%→5.3%这样快速飙升，而不5.25%→5.28%→5.24%→5.27%。
后者虽然利率依然很高，但久期波动率（duration volatility）消失了。
股票就可以重新交易：订单、收入、利润率、EPS revision、FCF，而不是每天交易US10Y。

3、这就是为什么“只要收益率稳定”，很多股票反而有可能出现一轮非常明显的补涨？
核心是盈利没有坏，FactSet在10月2日的Q3财报季预览显示，标普500 Q3预计将连续第三个季度实现 25%以上EPS增长。更重要的是市场对整个三季度Q3 EPS consensus反而上调了1.4%。
与此同时，标普500的forward PE已经从年初约22倍降到大约 19.2倍。

4、因此现在最好的美股环境其实不是“US10Y暴跌”
1）市场并不一定需要十年美债收益率从5.3%→4.5%，甚至长端收益率的这种走势未必是好事。因为如果10Y突然从5.3掉到4.5，原因无外乎是是失业率飙升、PMI暴跌、信用风险恶化、企业盈利下修等这样基本面恶化因素（当当然如果美伊真正缓和，油价大跌，长端收益率也能下行但不一定跌倒4.5%，更可能是5%上下晃荡）。

这种情景下，利率大幅下降，但是eps也会被大幅下修。小盘股、工业、银行、消费未必上涨。

2）真正理想的是金发姑娘Goldilocks式利率下降，例如5.30% → 5.20% → 5.10% → 5.05%
同时GDP仍有增长、就业温和放缓、工资压力下降、油价不再继续飙升、Fed暂停继续加息、企业EPS继续上修。

于是贴现率小幅走低，同时产业盈利继续向上，这才是对股票最舒服的组合。

简单说就是：
当下美股真正怕的不是5.2%~5.3%以上的10年期收益率本身，而是怕收益率继续快速向上重定价（5.3%左右快速飙升到5.5%甚至更高，如果这样大部分资产都被压制）。

过去一个多月10Y从4.7%左右冲到5.3%，更重要的是10年实际利率从2.4%左右升到接近3%。这相当于整个股票市场的真实贴现率突然被抬高了50bp。这种情景下 AI和大型科技靠盈利增长扛住了，所以指数看起来没什么问题；但等权标普、小盘、金融、房地产和大量传统行业已经发生了一轮明显的估值收缩。

这种情况下，并不需要10Y重新跌回4.5%,只要5.3%左右不再继续快速向上，同时企业盈利不下修，估值压缩就会逐渐缓解。这两天我们能看到的道指、标普等权也能小幅往上反弹，逻辑就在这里。

如果US10Y甚至缓慢回到5.2%上下，市场交易的重点会重新从“利率还要涨多少”，回到“谁的盈利还在增长”。最值得关注的可能反而是过去一个月业绩没有坏、EPS还在上修，却单纯被实际利率压掉估值的股票。

text:
Auday 1.0.1 is now live!

This update adds Japanese and Korean support for AI-generated content, including summaries, Highlights, daily Reflections and Chat replies. You can switch languages in Settings → AI Primary Language.

It also fixes the silent-recording issue affecting some Apple Watch Ultra users, improves transfer reliability between Apple Watch and iPhone, and brings a major overhaul of local storage for smoother loading and browsing as your recording history grows.

On launch day, Auday reached #1 in the App Store’s paid Lifestyle charts in multiple countries. The response has far exceeded our expectations, and every download, message and suggestion has been a huge encouragement. Behind Auday is a solo developer, working late to collect your feedback, investigate issues and keep improving the app. Thank you for your support and patience.

We also want to explain the choices behind transcription. To support a wider range of iPhones while keeping resource use low and minimizing slowdowns, our current on-device speech recognition model prioritizes speed and efficiency. In tests on iPhone 17 Pro, several hours of audio often took just a few seconds to transcribe. Actual performance varies with the device and recording. That speed comes with some accuracy trade-offs. Auday AI uses surrounding context when interpreting transcripts and generating content to help identify and work through recognition errors, reducing their impact on summaries, analysis and conversations.

For the next update, we plan to introduce an optional speech recognition model with higher accuracy and slightly higher resource requirements, alongside the current lightweight model. You’ll be able to switch between them and choose the balance of speed and accuracy that best suits your iPhone and your needs. We’ll also continue adding support for more languages.

To thank everyone for the support, we’re extending our 50% launch discount for one more week. Buy once, with no Auday subscription.

AppStore: https://t.co/VXAoQquioV

Thank you for being part of Auday’s beginning. We’ll keep listening and making it better.

This just comes as a strong reminder to many of us here on X and other social platforms that the industry in which we involve ourselves is a very evil one. Money will drive people to insane limits good or bad. 

@TraderJonesy made an excellent post about how more retail traders need to take responsibility for their own actions and not blame someone on X who may have given incorrect analysis or observation. Some people have nothing to lose and will go to insane and inhumane limits to get revenge on someone. It’s a sick and evil world we live in.

text:
if you’re trying out Grok @Bot for the first time today, I suggest first connecting apps that you use regularly so that your bot has enough context about the work you do, and  the tools it needs to do the job. for example, your calendar, slack, issue tracker, CRM, Google Drive etc

you don’t need to rush into making multiple bots! your primary bot is very capable even on its own. i’d even recommend doing everything with one bot first before you make new ones. the reason you might want to add new bots is for specialization and organization, but that can come later 

in a one bot setup, your bot does all the work that your normally do. when you have multiple bots, it’s more like having a team, and you can design that team in a way that matches how you like to best work. for example, if you work in GTM, you might want one bot to organize all work for a single customer. or you may want to have specialists that handle one small part of the overall workflow, like an Outreach bot

when you feel like it makes sense to add new bots to your team, check out our bot marketplace: https://t.co/VwX8eKMN1l 

or if you want to design your own, try my bot designer Dr Eggbot who can make you high quality bots: https://t.co/ajrjeHdzUO

text:
I got shellacked for this post back in March — but it turned out to be pretty prescient.

7 months of war later, Iran can’t completely close Hormuz — but it can make transits dramatically more expensive in economic and military terms.

1. The U.S. has committed 30% of the Navy to the Battle for Hormuz. 30%! 

Setting aside the budgetary costs, think of the opportunity costs: the training, maintenance, etc., being forgone to fight this war. 

By expending scarce military resources at an astounding rate, the U.S. is depleting its readiness and jeopardizing our capacity to handle contingencies that could genuinely threaten U.S. security — not just today, but well into the future.

Is it worth it? Certainly not.

2. Getting crewed vessels to run Hormuz is extremely expensive in hazard pay and insurance. Crews are collecting a massive premium (as they should) for risking their lives to cross the strait. Other rerouting efforts to avoid the Red Sea also add exorbitant transit costs, pushing up crude prices.

All of this is for Trump to avoid the indignity of paying Iran off with tolls, which would likely be much cheaper than the $15-$20 per barrel risk premium to cross Hormuz cited in recent Wall Street Journal coverage.

(Although the longer this goes on, the higher Iran can bid up the price for tolls, because we’re showing them we’re willing to pay $15-$20 extra to get oil out of Hormuz. Whereas Iran’s “ask” early in the war was a $1/barrel premium, it’s going to be much higher now, because markets have shown a willingness to pay.)

Bottom line: The Hormuz situation has not changed substantially since early in the war. Iran can drive up the costs and risks to traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, indefinitely. The U.S. can’t stop all attacks.

The only difference is that markets are finally adjusting to the new reality — shippers are moving oil despite attack — and pricing in higher risk as a result. 

Oil will flow from the region, but as long as this quagmire continues, prices will stay high, and the U.S. will waste its resources “securing” global oil prices of $100/barrel.

This situation was entirely unnecessary.

Congrats, Mr. Trump, on starting your first Forever War.

> @Coinbase tokenized equities → Data Streams for 24/5 market data

> UBS → DTA for tokenized fund subscriptions/redemptions

> DTCC → CRE + Chainlink infrastructure for collateral workflows

> 80+ Blockchain networks → CCIP

And the list goes on.

These look like very different use cases, but they're increasingly pieces of the same problem: how do you make financial assets actually usable once they're onchain?

Issuance gets the asset onchain. The infrastructure around it determines what you can actually do with it.
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
My @Chainlink thesis has changed quite a bit over the past year.

I used to think about it mostly as: Data → DeFi.

Then: Data + cross-chain connectivity → infrastructure for DeFi and tokenized assets.

I think even that framing is becoming outdated. Look at what Chainlink is actually building now:

> Data → What is the asset worth?
> CCIP → Where can it move?
> ACE → Who can use it?
> CRE → How do the systems coordinate?
> DTA → How is the fund operated?
> Fulcrum → How can the asset be financed?
> SVR → How can protocols recapture value from liquidations?
> Payment Abstraction → How does usage translate into network economics?

These aren't random product expansions. They're increasingly different parts of the same financial workflow. The Chainlink opportunity isn't "oracles become bigger", it's whether Chainlink becomes the standard orchestration layer between blockchains and the global financial system.

LINK:NYC should give us a lot more evidence either way.

text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

quoted_text:
Ben Affleck reveals he writes Python, understands convolutional neural networks, worked extensively with GPUs, and used his celebrity status to get private looks at Google and OpenAI’s video models

“I’ve always been kind of into computers since I was young. Then, when film started to move from analog film to digital, I became more interested in that aspect of it. The visual-effects workflow for many years has included machine learning, so I can write pretty shitty Python scripts and stuff like that.

“With convolutional neural networks, which were the precursors to what the transformer can do, which is much more computation simultaneously, you would do things like look at what’s called a tensor. That’s the numerical translation of a visual image in numbers, like the batch number, the frame number and the red, green and blue values of each pixel in each frame. It’s just that simple. That numeric is called a tensor.

“You’d use a convolutional neural network to identify patterns that reveal what’s called edge detection or feature extraction, which is identifying patterns well enough to know, this is where the window ledge is, so we can more easily take the green-screen image out and replace it with something.

“That was familiar to me early on because, prior to Artists Equity, I had a small visual-effects company. I’ve worked with GPUs a lot too. The visual-effects guys said, ‘Hey, you should see. There are a couple: Google and this other company, OpenAI, are doing really interesting stuff with transformers in video.’

“I’ve learned that I can actually just call up and go, ‘Hey, it’s Ben Affleck. Can I come see what you’re doing?’ Sometimes people say yes, to my astonishment.”

text:
IMD by @surfcoderepeat wants an idea to become a working financial application through a network of AI agents.

Its bigger ambition is for those agents to earn enough to keep building, eventually supporting companies managed entirely by the network.

That starts with two connected pieces: Identity MD NFTs organise the workforce, while the $IMD token connects payments and incentives.

Each of the 2,000  NFTs represents one swarm seat* Holders connect a machine running the IMD daemon and supply AI inference, the computation behind answers and code. The NFT lets an agent contribute to the network, although owning one doesn’t guarantee profitable work.

Customers bring that workforce an objective, such as building a vault and its website. The system checks the request and breaks it into implementation, testing, review and delivery with pricing is 0.5 IMD per request, paid on @Ethereum through x402.

When that work produces a token-bearing launch, the agents can participate in its economics.

- 2% of the new token’s supply goes to wallets with accepted launch work,
- 8% is allocated per connected seat at admission.

The requester controls the remaining 90% with their value depends on what gets built and whether anyone wants it.

The same workforce can also answer oracle questions for applications.

With chain evidence, agents propose calculations at fixed blocks, and the deployer reruns the agreed calculation before signing. A contract can verify that signature and the agreement count.

POOL4 connects its trading activity to funding.

When selling pushes IMD inventory above the protocol-owned pool’s cap, excess tokens and proportional ETH are removed.

- 85% of that IMD is earmarked for burning
- 4.5% for stakers
- 6% for orchestrator bonding
- 4.5% for NFT inference nodes

Stakers receive sIMD shares with growing IMD backing. Bonding would convert reserved tokens into ETH for computation, but bonding and node payouts remain unfinished.

As of October 5, swarm deployment remains Sepolia-only, while published work includes imdUSD documentation and Ember World audits.

However, there are some concerns like shared AI mistakes, deployer-dependent signing and unaudited POOL4 contracts remain substantial risks, including documented owner powers to withdraw liquidity and sweep staked IMD.

The encouraging part is that each useful application can give people another reason to use IMD and bring more work to the swarm. If that demand becomes recurring, it could help fund the agents that build the next application.

There’s still execution ahead, but the foundation is taking shape: a workforce, a payment token and a growing set of experiments.

Turning those experiments into products people keep using would bring IMD closer to its ambition of an economy that sustains its own builders.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
Pre Market Thoughts 7 Oct 26

No reprieve from yields as the long end continues inching up. For readers who were unaware about what i meant on the gilts long end in yesterday's note. A big of history - in 2022, Chancellor Kwasi unveiled a mini budget that was the final straw for the GBP bond market (gilts). The BOE (central bank of england) had to then stop in to intervene in the markets as the long end unwind threatened the collapse of pension schemes in a race to liquidation. At the height of the crisis, the 30Y gilt surged 160bps over 3 days... with a 120bp intraday range. On a zerocoupon bond, this would be a 30% move in the price of the bond itself....

Now i am not saying that we are going to explode up in yields and then subsequently collapse - policy interventions would determine the path that this situation unfolds. Instead, on a time horizon, i do feel that this is getting somewhat close, especially as the real economy and single name non-AI stocks are feeling the brunt of it.

In the SPX yesterday, utilities drove returns (https://t.co/hid91tI0Y5) - this helped to push the index to new highs while tech and semis languished. Interestingly, memory stocks were hit very hard especially into the lead up on the close. There has not been much news on this so i am not too sure where this move is originating from. I would not be very aggressive on buying this dip in memory until we get to 950s in MU.

The overall indexes have been much gentler to ride than individual stocks themselves. This is a theme i keep harping about. I think this dispersion will continue as rotations underneath the index continues.

In crypto, i made the call yesterday that markets might shock people by dipping just when everyone thinks that the "cycle bottom is in" - i continue to hold to that. Majors have very soggy price action while the alt momentum leaders are dying and rotating. Liquidity is also drying up on quotes and i think we are due for a move downwards.

My thoughts on TOKEN2049 thus far is that there is much less retail in the space now. instead there is alot more insitutional folks wandering around. This presents its own set of challenges and opportunities for the cycle ahead and i will talk more in a separate post.

Meanwhile the $PRL meet up was EXTREMELY shocking to me. I went there expecting a small niche meet up but i saw not only a huge crowd but many folks who have been early into narratives. I also saw many funds and overhead many conversations. Generally, this has been a very difficult token to buy and it seems like ...most people are still very underexposed.

The only venue to trade this has been safetrade. I spun up a venue earlier this year to trade $PRL - It is the lowest fee venue to accumulate $PRL on a orderbook basis. (https://t.co/OEFc0XbDJA) There is NO transaction fee taken for selling $PRL.

text:
介绍一下这个BIP-448

BIP-448 是一个系列的软分叉提案，目前是Draft状态。

它本身不改变区块大小、也不提高基础层吞吐量。它给 Tapscript 加三个操作码，这三个操作码分别是：

✅OP_TEMPLATEHASH（BIP 446）：把“花费这笔输出的那笔交易”的模板哈希压到栈上。脚本可以要求花费交易必须是预先约定的结构。今天二层协议靠所有人预先签好交易来模拟这件事。
✅OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK（BIP 348）：用 BIP 340 校验对任意消息的签名，不只是对当前交易。可以做委托、预言机证明，以及“可重新绑定”的签名。
✅OP_INTERNALKEY（BIP 349）：把 Taproot 内部密钥压到栈上，主要是给上面两种用法省字节，不是独立功能。

这几个BIP合在一起，能做成或明显简化很多事情：

1️⃣LN-Symmetry（以前叫 Eltoo）

2️⃣多方通道变得可能

3️⃣两人通道简化，比如Daric

4️⃣状态链（statechains）

5️⃣Ark 收款变成非互动，可以升级到Erk

6️⃣把现有闪电从HTLC升级到 PTLC 会简单很多

7️⃣延时金库

8️⃣DLC 的预签名变少

#BTC #BIP448 #LN #ARK #HTLC #PTLC #DLC #STATECHAIN

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Every trust mechanism in software comes down to one question. Who made the record.

A log is made by the system, afterwards, and it says what the system decided to write. An audit is made by a person, later, out of those logs. A proof is made by the computation, while it runs.

Nobody writes it. Nobody can edit it. That is the whole difference.

author: lagrangedev
quoted_text:
A signed log will tell you the right model ran. So will a signed log from a system that quietly ran a cheaper one and typed the expensive name into the file.

A proof cannot do that. Change the model, change the input, change one number in the output, and it stops verifying. There is no version of it that is wrong and still passes.

A claim can be honest and wrong. A proof cannot be wrong.

text:
Why I’m against TEE’s:  
 
TEEs conflict with blockchain's original ethos which was designed around the idea of “don't trust, verify.”

Traditional blockchain execution:  Anyone can independently verify that a computation was executed correctly.  Security comes from cryptography, consensus, and economic incentives.

How about TEE execution? 

Computation happens inside a protected hardware environment – such as Intel SGX. 

Outsiders can’t inspect the execution directly and instead have to rely on hardware-generated attestations that the expected code ran.

So rather than relying exclusively on decentralized verification – you're introducing trust in hardware manufacturers, firmware, attestation infrastructure, and the absence of exploitable hardware vulnerabilities.  

That introduces a messy form of centralized trust into a decentralized system.

And this is why @BaranosAI is different than anything out there.  

Maybe if they had a chain like @fogo they wouldn’t need the TEE workaround.

text:
Damn! 老马牛逼，Grok bot才是@SpaceXAI 的太子啊，
马斯克刚刚发布了一条足以改写 AI 格局，甚至震撼整个 AI 行业的的重磅声明：Grok Bot 不再绑死自家模型， 未来在处理任何具体任务时，系统将直接调度全网最顶级的后端模型，包括 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5、Midjourney、Suno 以及其他领先的 API。
唯一考核的标准只有一句话：怎么做最能给用户交付最好的结果。

这条以 SpaceX 官方名义发出的推文，在短短几小时内席卷了两千多万曝光， 很多人第一反应以为这是马斯克在变相承认自家模型的短板， 但只要看懂这背后的商业重构，你会发现这其实是一场极其冷酷的升维降击： 大模型打到底层，模型层正在退化为廉价的电力，而真正的超级霸主，正在疯狂抢夺总插座和电表的垄断权。

马斯克这次点名的三家，精准踩中了目前通用大模型依然无法完全吃下的三个顶级专科：
 写复杂代码与长程 Agent，直接调度口碑最好的 Claude Opus 5.5；
 做高审美视觉设计，直接调用统治力依然稳固的 Midjourney；
 生成音乐与音频，直接挂载完成度最高的 Suno。

这背后撕开了未来 AI 竞争最值钱的四个底层真相：
第一，护城河从我们模型最聪明，彻底变成了我们最知道该叫谁。 底层的模型权重每隔六个月就会迭代一次，天天跟同行卷跑分是无休止的军备消耗； 但只要用户的任务历史、工具授权、记忆上下文和订阅入口全部沉淀在 Grok Bot 这个壳子里， 底下换谁的脑子，用户根本不在乎，马斯克依然稳稳收走所有的月费和流量。

第二，专科模型没有死，但生存形态彻底变了。 马斯克愿意花钱为画图和写歌单独接外部 API，说明垂直工具在极致审美上依然有壁垒； 但未来垂直工具的终极宿命，不再是逼用户单独下载一个新 App，而是变成顶级路由平台随时调用的一行接口。

第三，代理层比模型层更接近终极收费点。 模型可以月月换代，价格可以被开源打到脚脖子， 但那个能帮你自动规划步骤、记住你的习惯、管理几十个工具权限并在后台默默把成品交回来的主控智能体，才是谁也偷不走的刚需资产。

第四，这也是一场算力与分发的隐秘对冲。 今年 5 月 Anthropic 刚刚签下了使用 SpaceX 旗下 Colossus 超级算力集群的协议； 在前端把流量路由给 Claude，在后端卖算力给 Anthropic， 这根本不是单向的认输，而是一场把算力、分发与模型三方利益吃干抹净的平台级阳谋。

这其实给所有做产品、做内容的朋友提了个极其清醒的原则： 
以后别再盲目死磕某一家大模型的单向崇拜了。 聪明人的工作流早已按任务彻底解耦： 写代码挂 Claude，做图挂 Midjourney，整理挂本地， 把你的忠诚度留给最终的交付结果，而不是任何一个具体的模型厂牌。

大家平时用 AI 时，是习惯死守一个工具用到底，还是已经学会了根据任务把不同模型组合起来用了，欢迎分享交流鸭！

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
🗿 Beyond Chain Boundaries: The Next Layer of DeFi

Stonfiers! Have you ever thought about what the next step in DeFi could look like — and whether it’s really about moving users between chains? What if, instead, those boundaries simply became invisible? 

That was the question Andrey Fedorov, CMO & CBDO at STONfi Dev, explored at HSC Conference in Seoul, where he shared our perspective on the future of cross-chain infrastructure and DeFi.

Here are a few key ideas from the talk:

✨ Why do we need cross-chain swaps at all?
Different ecosystems have different strengths: TON brings distribution inside Telegram, TRON has strong stablecoin activity, and Ethereum offers deep liquidity and settlement. The opportunity is to connect these ecosystems — without asking users to navigate between them manually.

✨ What would a better cross-chain experience look like?
Instead of finding liquidity, moving assets, and then executing a transaction themselves, users could simply request an outcome. The infrastructure would source the liquidity and handle the execution in the background.

✨ How does Omniston fit into this model?
Omniston puts this approach into practice through a network of resolvers that compete to provide quotes, with native-to-native execution and atomic settlement ensuring that users receive what they approved — or the transaction reverts.

✨ What does the future of cross-chain look like?
Cross-chain execution becomes a capability built into financial products rather than a destination users have to navigate. Users, applications, and liquidity no longer need to exist in the same ecosystem — different networks can work together as one financial environment.

The future isn’t one chain. It’s one financial experience across many of them.

#STONfi #CrossChain #TON #DeFi

Its a GREAT DAY for humanity and math.

AI as math genie: If you asked a mathematician anywhere from 5000 BCE to a Jan 2026 AD whether they would like a math genie to exist, 100% of the mathematicians would have said yes. 

Mathematicians as altruists: Mathematicians give up significant opportunity cost to help advance human knowledge. Its a no brainer they will eventually adjust to this new world and be glad this happened - it is just an extreme but temporary shock to "i am world class at math" as an identity. 

The most important things to do asap. 
1) Scale ambition 100x: We need to totally recalibrate what problems are solvable as researchers. 
2) Open safe models: We need frontier models to be widely available in the open AND be safe. 
3) Open frontier research: Make AI based frontier research widely accesible in an open, collab. setting.

the two reasons usually given for why tokenizing private credit makes sense:

issuer side: distribution

holder side: novel access to yield sources, and making that yield productive via composability

the underrated one is liquidity

for these assets to be underwritten and become productive, curators and leveraged carry traders need to be able to exit atomically

but private credit has duration baked in, tokenized or not.

in tradfi private credit is mostly illiquid and you can only redeem periodically

once tokenized, programmability and atomic settlement allow global secondary markets to emerge very efficiently

variable rate fixed income assets with a steadily rising share price is non volatile by nature. 

AMMs are very well suited for this, no divergence loss in normal times and far more competitive for the issuer than a mandated active MM
