winstek, a taiwan chip-test house with NT$2.7B of revenue in the first half, just approved NT$13.4B of 2026 capex. its plan in december was NT$5.6B.

one of the quieter squeezes in AI chips right now is testing them.

its parent sigurd said at an oct 6 briefing (per taiwan press) that it is raising test prices, and that customers are locking capacity with guarantee agreements and testers reserved just for them.

why: an AI accelerator sits on the tester far longer than a phone chip. advantest says accelerators need "longer test times and additional insertions" as 3D packaging gets more complex. more chips x more minutes each = tester hours run out.

in the path:
- KYEC: lifted 2026 capex to a record NT$50B in april
- sigurd and winstek
- advantest (japan), which makes the testers: raised its full-year sales forecast ~21% in july 
- teradyne $TER 

imo testing looks like packaging did 2 years ago: a step few people model until customers start reserving it.

advantest and teradyne report later this month.

text:
India needs @Starlink 🇮🇳

• 11,256 of India’s listed villages still lacked 4G coverage as of May 2026.

• India had 1.093 billion internet subscriptions in March 2026, but only 440.87 million were rural. Rural subscription density was 48.31 per 100 people, compared with 126.80 in urban India.

• BharatNet had laid over 850,000 route-km of fibre and made about 221,000 Gram Panchayats service-ready. However, its Points of Presence were reported operational at only 80,472 Gram Panchayats in June 2026.

• Only 4.26% of India’s internet subscriptions were wired connections in March 2026. Starlink could give underserved communities another route to high-speed broadband.

• Starlink has already built 20 gateway sites in India, according to SpaceX Vice President of Starlink Business Operations Lauren Dreyer, speaking at India Mobile Congress today.

• Starlink says it has developed India-specific security controls designed to keep Indian user data within India.

• Its satellite network could bring high-speed internet to remote villages, mountains and islands where extending fibre or mobile networks is difficult.

• Better connectivity could help rural schools access online learning, clinics offer remote consultations and small businesses reach more customers. Starlink already supports education and healthcare in remote communities internationally.

• Portable Starlink terminals have supported disaster response around the world. They could give Indian emergency teams backup connectivity when floods, earthquakes or storms damage ground networks.

• Direct to Cell could also help ordinary 4G phones connect beyond tower coverage, subject to Indian approvals and mobile operator partnerships.

• The government itself identifies difficult terrain, low commercial viability and infrastructure constraints as reasons for remaining coverage gaps. This is exactly where Starlink could help India reach more people.

• India should complete the remaining clearances and spectrum allocation so Starlink can begin commercial service.

• SpaceX’s Vice President of Starlink Business Operations, Lauren Dreyer, said that Starlink is ready to help achieve Prime Minister Modi’s vision of 100% connectivity across India. She highlighted its potential to connect remote classrooms, support telemedicine and restore connectivity after disasters, adding, “With Starlink, people can get connected within minutes, not years.”

India’s hardest-to-reach communities deserve reliable internet too.

The stakes around data are changing.
As artificial intelligence moves into everything, the demands on our data compound. So do the risks.
We now share our ideas, intentions, and reasoning with these systems. The skills and experience that we’ve spent a lifetime building. For institutions and builders, it’s their competitive intelligence, their proprietary insights. The edge that separates winners from everyone else. Data is our most valuable asset.
This is also a moment of massive opportunity. Agentic AI has the potential to create new abundance for humanity. But for that future to be possible, agents need data that makes them capable. Data they control, that moves with them across applications, and that they can independently verify. As owners, we’ll need to prove to regulators what our agents did. All things that today’s infrastructure cannot provide.
Sui represents the first half of the solution. A coordination layer built for the machine economy. Walrus is the data platform that completes it.
Walrus makes data a first-class asset. The terms of access and monetization stay with its owner, not a vendor. It empowers builders to ship agents and apps without locking themselves or their customers into any model or platform. Users carry their data, their memory, and their work across systems while cryptographic proof replaces vendor trust. Everything is anchored on Sui: a coordination layer and a data layer built to move as one.
Welcome to the new era of Walrus. The data platform built for the demands of AI.

The internet’s business model was built around people: attention, ads, subscriptions and checkout. AI agents are changing that. They can retrieve and use content without sending a human reader back to the publisher.

That raises a real question for creators, publishers and developers: how can they get paid when an agent uses their work, sometimes for a fraction of a cent?

Our new Coinbase Institute @CoinbaseCBI paper, "Machine-to-machine payments in the AiFi era," examines why existing payment rails often struggle with high-velocity microtransactions—and why stablecoins on low-cost networks are a strong fit today.

The policy goal should be an open, interoperable payment layer, with safeguards that match the risks—not closed marketplaces that decide who can participate.

author: gregthegreek
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Crypto’s next adoption wave starts when you don’t have to explain how to use it.

@litocoen

“I think today is the time where the mobile UX is finally at a point where you can really onboard a normie without having to explain anything.

Obviously, mobile apps existed in crypto before, like Binance or Coinbase. But I’m talking purely about non-custodial crypto here, which is much harder to abstract away for all kinds of reasons.

And so that is not the case anymore.

You mentioned FOMO. I think it’s crazy how, once you see a product that is really well constructed from a UX point of view, how quickly it can actually scale to a million, two million users.

When there’s no barrier to entry anymore, it just spreads like wildfire. One person tells the other, ‘Use this. You can trade and make money.’

Maybe in our case, it will be, ‘Use this. You can spend with a card and get cashback. Or put your money there regardless of where you are in the world, and you’ll earn some earn rate that is higher than your local bank.’

So once you have a form factor that is really intuitive, mobile apps can spread in a very viral way that a desktop app like Rabby will just never.”

Host:

“Yeah, totally agree. And not to harp on this too long, but I would say I was the case that you had to win over for mobile, because I’m this desktop-only guy for life with crypto.

I never thought I’d do serious crypto on a mobile app, but I’ve completely pivoted that stance.

I think there’s a huge inflection point for crypto adoption because you need to be able to get customers when they’re commuting to work on the bus, or they’re walking, or doing something where they’re carrying their phone. They’re away from desktop.

You’ve just opened the aperture for way more user interaction, and I do think it’s going to be huge.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

可能很多人跟我有同一个困扰，「钱明明是自己的，为什么用起来，还得在几个 App 之间搬来搬去？」

今天在新加坡 #TOKEN2049 现场，听 Dr. Han @Han_Gate 介绍 Gate Money，我想到的就是这个问题！🧐

平时我们买币用交易所，买股票用券商，收款用银行，出国消费再找一张能用的VISA卡。每个工具单独看都没什么问题，连起来用，就开始折腾：开户、转账、换汇、等到账……

这次“One Gate. Everything Money.” ，就是解决这个问题，将法币、Crypto、股票、ETF、黄金，以及银行账户和支付等服务，全部连接到同一个账户体系里。资产配置、兑换、消费，可以在一个 App 内完成所有操作。

目前 #Gate App更新到 v8.39.0 就能直接体验。简单拆解一下，今天现场发布几个让我觉得十分性感的创新点，以及我个人的一些思考：

1️⃣ 全球同名银行账户，一键在线开通

像我这种平时资金基本都在 Web3和钱包里面，而银行卡里常年没几个钱的人，以前出金收汇要在好几个平台、中转行之间来回倒，麻烦不说还极易踩雷。现在符合条件地区的用户在 App 内填完资料就能一键生成本人名下的全球电子银行账户，目前支持美金，英镑，欧元等，未来会支持更多，这对于常年海外生活的人，及其方便。银行转账和加密资产可以直接互转，合规与体验一步到位。

2️⃣ 打破资产壁垒

过去我们的资产是割裂的，炒股的在券商，Crypto 在交易所或者钱包，现金在银行，黄金在大宗账户。想花股票里的钱，得先挂单卖出、T+N 结算、提现到银行卡，再去消费。

Gate Money 直接把法币、Crypto、美股、ETF、黄金和支付全塞进了一个 App。最绝的是资产可以直接拿来消费，持有的股票或加密资产不用提前卖出，刷 Gate Card（支持 Apple Pay 和Google Pay）直接划扣结算。从“用 BTC 买披萨”到“用 NVDA 股票买咖啡”，资产的流动性彻底被盘活了。

3️⃣ 流动性与收益两不误

闲置在账户里的法币和活期资产，不用锁仓就能享受高达 3.6% 的年化收益，保持资金随时可用的同时又能持续产生 现金流，真正做到了让“资产持续增长，价值随时流动”。

💡 个人现场的一些思考

传统金融的核心问题不是缺少资产，而是资产被“深深锁在墙内”；Web3 的痛点不是缺乏创新，而是难以无缝渗透进日常 Web2 消费场景。

Gate 这次不只是做了一个整合版钱包，而是利用其在全球 81 个受监管司法辖区的合规牌照，包括马耳他 MiCA/PSD2、迪拜 VARA 等。以及底层清算网络，构建了一套通用的资产结算基础设施。

对于整个行业来说，这种“账户无界”的模式极大概率会触发新一轮的产品迭代潮。它让 Web3 从单纯的“交易场景”，演变成一个覆盖个人全球资产配置、跨境收付款、日常消费与理财的终极个人金融终端。

从开户 ➔ 资金 ➔ 资产 ➔ 消费，金融的边界终于被抹平了。不得不说，这一波传统金融与数字资产的一体化整合，格局确实拉满了🔥。后续期待一下，具体的落地细节，比如哪些地区能开通，转账多久能到账，换汇总成本是多少，支付能不能稳定成功等等。持续关注！🧐

text:
相爱？相杀？Binance Circle 和 OKX — — 我个人眼中的三角关系

众所周知，Circle 最大的大腿很长时间都是 Coinbase ，而 Coinbase 的主要市场一直在 欧美 ，而 USDC 在 Binance 和 OKX 很长一段时间都是不温不火的状态，虽然有交易对，但是都和 USDT 差距甚远。

而就在最近一周即传出了 Binance 投资 Circle 的新闻，也传出了 Circle （和其他企业一起）投资 OKX 的新闻，两则新闻都是真的，我就看到有小伙伴在问，那么是不是 Binance 和 Coinbase 都间接变成了 OKX 的股东？

如果是从财务角度来看，确实可以理解为有了一层间接的股权利益关系。Coinbase 和 Binance 持有 Circle 的股份，Circle 又持有 OKX 的股份，那么 Circle 将来从 OKX 获得的投资收益，也可能让 Coinbase 和 Binance 间接受益。

当然，OKX 的股东是 Circle，这不代表 Coinbase 和 Binance 可以直接参与 OKX 的经营。

而这层关系带来的变化，是 Binance 和 Coinbase 的部分利益，开始和竞争对手的业务联系在一起。假设 OKX 发展得更好，Circle 持有的 OKX 股权也因此升值，那么即使 Coinbase 和 Binance 没有从 OKX 获得一个用户，也可能通过 Circle 分享一部分收益。

Binance 投资 Circle 本身也是同样的道理。以前推广 USDC，收益主要取决于双方的商业合作，现在除了合作收入，又增加了股权收益。按照这次披露的五年协议，Circle 会根据约定钱包中的 USDC 持有余额，向 Binance 支付月度激励费。而 Circle 股权的价值，则还受到 USDC 在其他平台的发展，以及 Circle 其他业务的影响。

对 Circle 来说，投资 OKX 也增加了一种收益来源。原来双方合作，主要是让 USDC 在 OKX 上被更多人使用，现在如果 OKX 本身发展得好，Circle 也有机会通过持股受益。所以同样是扩大 USDC 的使用，Binance 是拿自己的钱投资发行方，Circle 则是拿自己的钱投资交易平台，两边增加的股权收益来自不同的业务。

而对 OKX 来说，除了获得资金，也让 Circle 的利益和平台本身联系得更紧了。过去 Circle 更关心 USDC 在 OKX 上被多少人使用，现在 OKX 整体的发展，也会影响 Circle 的投资回报。即使有些业务并不使用 USDC，只要能提高 OKX 的价值，Circle 作为股东也有机会受益，这就给双方继续投入资源合作，多了一个理由。

所以这几家的利益并不是完全一致，但也不再只有竞争。Binance 和 Coinbase 仍然希望用户留在自己的平台，Circle 则希望 USDC 在更多平台被使用，OKX 希望合作能带来更多用户和交易。

现在通过股权把这些关系连接起来以后，就出现了一个有意思的结果，同一个用户在 OKX 交易，手续费由 OKX 赚，但这部分业务如果最终提高了 Circle 所持股权的价值，Binance 和 Coinbase 也可能间接受益。

下一篇，我会聊聊我眼中，为什么“OKX 为什么会接受 Circle 的投资 而不是 投资 Circle”。

text:
UNSOLVED SINCE 1968: A QUESTION ABOUT ODD LITTLE SHAPES

Back in 1968, the German mathematician Heinrich Heesch asked a question nobody needed answered. If a shape can't tile a floor forever, how many times can you surround it with copies of itself before the rings jam?

Most shapes jam fast. For shapes built only from squares, hexagons or triangles, the best anyone has found is 4 rings.

The current best on https://t.co/sb9WmYYSXj is a shape made of 15 hexagons. It gets through 4 full rings and covers 251 of the 254 cells in the 5th. Then a machine-checked proof says it can never go further.

Now mathematicians and researchers are digging into what it would take to close those last few gaps. Dr. Bartosz Naskręcki, @nasqret, has been helping lead that effort, working through candidates and ideas with contributors in public.

Getting to a complete 5th ring wouldn't just top the leaderboard. It would be a new mathematical result.

Nearly 60 years on, people are still chasing it.

Every attempt is rechecked from scratch and posted publicly and anyone can try. Multiplayer autoresearch, with humans and AI agents taking shots at the same unsolved problem.

#SUI 7月当时还在0.75美金时候，我说它是市场中最低估的公链！🧐

今天 #Sui Basecamp 第一天逛下来，更加坚定了我的想法，而且今天1.1美金，依旧十分性感，我任然可以坚定的说，它还是最低估的公链之一！

讲讲今天活动现场的观察和思考，信息量确实有点炸。帮大家梳理几个最硬核的看点，看看 Sui 到底在布局什么：

1️⃣ 4000万 TPS：不是为人类测的，而是给 AI 准备的。

现场直接主网实测，TPS 跑到了 4061 万（@CertiKCommunity 现场验证）。很多人可能会问：Visa 峰值才 6.5 万 TPS，人类哪用得着这么快？

答案是：未来交易的可能不是人，而是 AI Agents。人类等 3 秒刷卡无所谓，但 AI 代理在一秒钟内就要处理成千上万笔可能小到几厘钱的微支付，3 秒对 AI 来说就像一个光年。Sui 这次的定位非常清晰，要做未来 AI 经济的“信任底座”。

2️⃣ 原生 BTC 借贷 + 机构入场 (Hashi)

Hashi 这个协议很猛，不用把比特币包装成各种衍生代币，直接用原生 BTC 当抵押品去借贷。目前还没上线，承诺资金就已经破了 5 亿美元。更关键的是，他们拿下了获得美国联邦特许的加密银行 Anchorage Digital，未来机构用户在 Anchorage 里面点一下，就能把资金存进 Hashi 金库开始借贷。

3️⃣通缩信号：SUI 数量可能永远到不了 100 亿

台上提到了一个非常关键的机制：随着稳定币通过 Hashi 这些管道大量流入 Sui，产生的收益将用来直接回购 SUI。官方原话是：“一开始说总量上限 100 亿枚，但以后它恐怕永远也到不了 100 亿了，只会越来越少。” 这种持续的销毁和回购预期，对代币的长期价值是个极大的利好。

4️⃣基础设施全线铺开

除了性能，这次还一口气发了四项专门给 AI 和安全护航的基础设施：

阿里云合作：搞定 AI 代理的自主支付；
Google Cloud 合作：推出 VAA 可信身份验证；
Sui Threat Intelligence：实时检测加上自动化遏制，把安全防线拉满；
Walrus Console @WalrusProtocol 上线：给 AI 应用数据做存储和连接的中心枢纽。
值得提一嘴的是，@tradeonhudi 早上交易赛十分精彩，期待一下，SUI 在社交化perp dex领域的后发优势。

总结一下：以前大家聊公链，还在卷人类用户的体验；而 Sui 今天直接把格局拉到了下一个世代，打造一个让 AI 代理替人类处理金融资产的全套基础设施。

极其充实的一天，拭目以待 Basecamp 后面还有什么大招 ！💧💧💧

text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

最近一个月的复盘贴，也发点思考大干货

推特几乎没涨粉，因为除了一开始的打通Codex和ChatGPT Pro的教程之外没有发什么干货。剩下的时间我一直在做抖音，迭代优化代充网站代码，并思考自媒体、流量和商业变现之间的关系。

下面就想到哪里说哪里了，算分享，也算定期的思考记录，不过能够确保都是优质信息。

1、未来社媒平台账号是很重要的资产，无论是内容账号还是素人白号。

比如可以给每一个 KOL 或者产品账号都配备几个 KOC 名额，也就是所谓的自己当自己的水军。

2、目前 Opus 5.5 以及各大视频skill 的出现，让 AI 做视频并赢得流量成为可能。并且从根本上来讲，至少半年内平台不会封杀纯 AI 做的账号，所以，AI矩阵号可做。

我也正在打造自己的内容生产系统，后续实现全自动化产出 AI 类账号

3、做自媒体 IP 比内容更重要。这里不是说内容不重要，而是说 IP 带来的信任度是无可比拟的，有了 IP，变现会更加容易。

所以，最好的方式是一个露脸的活人感账号，加几个数字人 AI 类账号

SEO的出海 SaaS 也要做，这个算另一个保底的收入，毕竟只有收入多元化之后，抗风险的能力才会更强。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
The October 7 atrocity was made especially foul because it came during the celebration of Simchat Torah. It was meant to be a time for unbridled joy in the scriptures—God’s gift to the Jewish people, the Jewish people’s gift to Western civilization and the world. It marks a complete cycle of Torah readings and the beginning of a new one.

On this anniversary of the attacks I think it’s worth remembering what the people killed that day were celebrating, why we who live on should join in defiantly celebrating still, as well as mourning. 

To seek the law of God is perhaps the most essentially human act, a way of honoring our sacred place at the hinge point of heaven and earth. We ask what is right—not simply right now, or right for a few, but right for all and for all time—because we are material beings drawn up by love into communion with eternal truth. 

To be overcome with awe and delight at the impossible good fortune in this high honor of being human is what simchat torah means, I think. It’s why the spirit of inhumanity is furious everywhere with desire to snuff such celebration out, and always has been. It’s why the Jewish people celebrate still, and why I for one am filled with sorrow in their sorrow, and joy in their abiding joy.

text:
前 Cursor 核心工程师、现 xAI 软件工程师 Lauren（@poteto）刚刚公开了她一个人单月合入 2500 个真实生产环境 PR 的超级工作流，并把全套配置做成了 Cursor 官方插件里的 poteto-mode。

一个月手搓 2500 个 PR，相当于一个程序员在三十天里，平均每天向正式代码库交付八十多个高质量功能与补丁， 一个人直接打出了一整支顶尖工程特战队的恐怖产能。

很多人以为这又是靠写长篇提示词去碰运气的玄学， 但只要翻看她开源出来的这套实战配置，你会发现这根本不是简单的写代码，而是一套把多模型分工、后台异步执行与自动化盯盘做到极致的现代化工程操作系统。

整套工作流里最值钱、最值得每个写代码的朋友立刻抄作业的，是这三个底层的硬核设计：

第一，按工种把模型彻底解耦，绝不拿同一个模型包打天下。 在她的配置里，写核心代码与算法实现，默认挂载极速且深度推理的 Grok 4.7 Extra High Fast； 而需要写复杂文档、做架构决策、或者进行复杂逻辑审查时，自动无缝切到 Claude Opus 5.5。 代码要快要硬，判断要准要深，两套脑子各司其职。

第二，把所有 Agent 强制赶去后台静默运行。 开启 run in background 选项，把上下文从主会话里剥离出来，只传文件路径，不内联长篇大论的代码片段； 程序员只负责在主干上规划架构、发号施令， 几十个子任务在后台互不干扰地并发推进，彻底终结了坐在屏幕前看着光标一个字一个字蹦出来的低效等待。

第三，也是最绝的杀手锏：全自动 PR 保姆工作流（Babysit Playbook）。 在真实开发中，写完代码往往只完成了 30%，剩下的全是改 CI 报错、对齐 Lint、回复 Review 机器人这类繁琐的脏活； 她配置了一套自动盯盘机制，只要输入一句检查某个 PR， 后台 Agent 会自动监听 GitHub Actions 的报错日志，自己读错误、自己提补丁、直到把所有的红灯全部跑成绿灯，不需要人肉反复插手。

这其实给所有做技术、写代码的朋友指明了一条极度确定的生产力进化路径： 未来的顶级程序员，早已不再是坐在键盘前敲语法的打字员， 而是指挥着多模型矩阵、在后台并发调度上百个自动化流水线的系统总司令。

把繁琐的修 Bug、跑测试和语法实现交给模型， 把你的脑力，全部留给真正有价值的架构设计与业务突破。

铁汁们在平时用 Cursor 或 Claude Code 写代码时，最耗费你时间的是哪一步？是写核心功能、还是反复改 CI 报错和修环境？ 欢迎交流分享呀～

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

The assets themselves were sound, but banks were closed for the weekend and redemptions had to wait until Monday. USDC slid between 90 cents and put positions across onchain finance in jeopardy.

No matter their reason, redemption delays are a pervasive risk area in onchain finance, a result of the "real-time" liquidity promise of blockchains vs. the realities of offchain capital.

When no one prices the risk, everyone is at risk.

text:
KRYVAN Nodes — A Different Approach

Nodes aren't new to crypto.

We've seen several versions over the years, and many eventually ran into the same problem: the rewards weren't supported by enough real economic activity.

Projects like StrongBlock showed how powerful the node idea could be. Buy a node, hold it and receive rewards.

But many early models depended heavily on continued growth. More people had to join, more nodes had to be sold and new capital helped support existing rewards.

It worked while growth continued. When growth slowed, the economics became difficult to sustain.

Then came nodes connected to gaming, validators and other ecosystems. The model changed, but another problem appeared: inflation.

You could receive thousands of tokens in rewards, but if millions of new tokens were constantly entering circulation, those rewards were being diluted.

That's what I want KRYVAN to approach differently.

Nodes should participate in the economy, not become the economy.

KRYVAN isn't being built around selling nodes.

We're building the products first: Play Arena, Market Arena, spectator participation, tournaments and eventually more competitive experiences.

$KRVN connects those experiences.

Instead of:

Sell nodes → pay rewards → sell more nodes

the goal is:

Build products → attract users → generate activity → create fees → burn and distribute value.

If KRYVAN grows, node holders should benefit from activity happening inside the ecosystem — not because another person bought another node.

Fixed nodes. Fixed supply.

There will be a limited number of KRYVAN nodes.

The current model allocates 10% of the total $KRVN supply to node holders, distributed in phases.

These are the people taking some of the earliest risk on KRYVAN, so I believe they should have meaningful alignment with the ecosystem.

But the supply remains fixed.

If nodes remain unsold, my current thinking is simple: those nodes disappear.

Their associated $KRVN allocation would also be removed from the node allocation and burnt.

Scarcity only matters if you respect it.

Where do future rewards come from?

This is the important part.

A node shouldn't require infinite token emissions to survive.

Once the initial node allocation has been distributed, the long-term model should increasingly depend on KRYVAN itself.

Play Arena can generate fees.

Market Arena can generate fees.

Spectators and tournaments create activity.

Token transactions and node transfers can generate fees.

Future products can add new sources of activity.

Part can go toward node holders, part can be burned and part can support the ecosystem.

The exact percentages still need to be modelled.

But the principle is simple:

real usage should create the rewards.

If KRYVAN grows, the economy around the nodes grows with it.

If usage doesn't grow, rewards shouldn't magically come from endless token printing.

That's the real experiment.

I don't want the main question about a KRYVAN node to be:

"How many tokens does it print every day?"

I want it to become:

"How much activity is happening across KRYVAN?"

More players. More games. More Market Arena participation. More spectators. More tournaments. More reasons to use $KRVN.

That's where the economics should come from.

Not infinite inflation.

Not endless node sales.

Not depending on the next buyer to pay the previous one.

Nodes can help bootstrap KRYVAN and reward the people who supported it early.

But KRYVAN shouldn't need to keep selling nodes to keep the model alive.

Build the product first. Build an economy people actually use. Then let nodes participate in the value that economy creates.

Crypto has already tried the infinite-emission node model.

I'd rather build something different.

Grok bot和Muse邪修大法：

1. 装 Pi Agent，重活丢给第三方免费模型  
在 Muse 里装 Pi Agent，模型走蚂蚁百灵 Ling 这类开放平台免费额度（每天约 50 万 token）。长文、写代码、批处理走外部免费模型，Muse 自己的周额度留给必须用 Muse Spark 的步骤。

2. 监控 Cloudflare 用量，防止账单爆炸  
Worker 免费档大约每天 10 万请求，家宽链式、中继、归档一旦被扫或被 Bot 轮询，很容易打穿。让 Agent 用官方模板建只读用量查询，设日请求和 CPU 时间阈值，超了就告警。

3. Muse Video 做竖屏素材，人审后再发小红书  
免费额度每周大约能出 20–30 条，加上邀请额度非常够用。适合脚本、分镜、口播底片。

4. 搭配落地 IP 跑 Claude Code

5. 搭配回国代理，做闲鱼管家  

6. 用 Tailscale 对 Muse、Grok Bot、家里机器组网 
Muse 有原生 Tailscale 连接器。组网后用 MagicDNS 互访，重活放家里或已有 VPS 上，Muse 做编排。

7. Cookie 同步解决云浏览器的登录墙  
本机扩展导出已登录站点的 session cookie，同步进 Bot/Muse 的 Chrome，实现无密码登录。

8. 把 Muse 额度接到 Grok Bot
用 muse2api 让 Grok Bot 消耗 Muse 的 token 写代码、生图、生视频。

9. 定时任务
Muse 用 Scheduled Tasks / Goals，Grok Bot 用 Routine。

10. Grok 多 Bot 分工，Muse 做生活管家
Grok 适合养收件、写代码、运营多个 Bot，共用一台云电脑的文件和登录态。Muse 用于邮件、日历、采购这类生活流程。

text:
OpenAI’s math release is, in the words of Opus, “the single most consequential mathematical release ever” *

LLMs have how made substantial progress on 4 of 7 Millenium Prize problems: Navier-Stokes (claimed), Riemann, Hodge and Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer. Poincaré was solved in 2003. The two left are P v NP and Yang Mills.
*conditional on verification

On average, each OpenAI result used only 3hrs of thinking compute on their new unreleased models.

Two years ago, models said 9.11 > 9.9. Today, we have results that the smartest human minds have not been able to achieve in their entire lives. It is clear that data, compute and algorithms scale. Every model generation (3mos) has made substantial intelligence progress.

It also becomes incredibly hard to not believe that all knowledge work will change monumentally over time. The things AI can not do in the foreseeable future are very likely context-bound (don’t have access to the right information) than intelligence bound. Some might argue they are also creativity-bound or judgement-bound (what should I work on), although it can be argued that future generations could solve for this (given, say, the advancement in research taste for models over time).

AGI is defined as surpassing human capabilities on virtually all cognitive tasks. By most interpretations of that definition, we are there. The domains humans are still better than AI, such as, robotics / physical world control (data-bound?), natural science research (data-bound), some creative domains like writing, movies, music (creativity-bound), super long tasks (context-bound), choosing problems to solve (creativity-bound) and maybe human relationships management (meat-proxy bound?).
In many ways, we have achieved AGI.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
I don't believe static drawdown and balance based daily loss limits are going to be sustainable methods of running a prop firm. I'm pretty much making it my mission to make sure they're not. I'll explain.

Static / balance based drawdowns rely on gambling mentality. Traders coming in, paying, failing, then repeating using max size. There is no edge here. It's called Gambler's Fallacy.

The ability to actually A-book is low, almost non-existent. Those that are showing the ability to A-book are probably doing it purely for marketing. And the reason is two-fold:
1. a prop firm's position can get liquidated while the trader maintains their funded status. Pretty simply, you can take insane leverage, you're not judged intraday. They could live capital intraday while you recover by end of day.
2. the rules don't limit bounds for risky behavior, reducing predictability. This requires equity-based drawdowns to have proper behavioral alignment.

I don't believe this is a sustainable model. Specifically, because trader's will have access to agentic models and these prop firms won't be able to A-book. Many of them don't allow API access for a reason, to ensure more sophisticated systems can't run but it won't matter. Agents can control DOMs and run anyway. 

Simply, this model will be run dry. 

We've spent more than a year now coming up with how to best use agents to build strategies. Think of it as your own quant firm. These systems understand risk, review institutional data, propose hypothesis with you, reject overfitting, have proper splits, run fully automated providing you notifications, and continuously look to improve. Simply, they build strategies the right way. It's what I run right now on Vanta with a $1M Pro account. And we're going to open it up to everyone in the next month. Over time, everyone will be able to use our systems to beat the firms. This has been my focus. I want you as a trader to build better strategies and give you the infra & tools to do so.

Prop firms should want you to succeed. They should be a capital layer that scales you up with the right incentive alignment. The majority of their distributed sim capital should be A-booked. We see the future because the future is now. Giving you the infra to build better strategies, giving you the right incentive to scale up, and A-booking. Everything else to me is a broken model.

Slept on this so I didn't reply purely on visceral instinct because framed a certain way, calling seed checks "option bets" feels like a direct attack on what founders and early-stage investors build every day. Some thoughts:

- Harry knows how to stir shit up for maximum engagement, so take the clip's framing with a grain of salt. @venkyganesan is a high-integrity world-class investor with undeniable pattern recognition. Both things can be true.
- We are at that point in the venture cycle where discourse is getting twitchy and folks are quick to trade jabs. Sharp elbows might win headlines, but winning at all costs comes at a cost.
- Investors deploy capital. Founders commit their time. From a pure portfolio construction lens (h/t Annie Duke), seed checks do look like asymmetric option calls, and LPs trust us to make them. But spreadsheet math should not obscure the human effort behind the business.
- Pure pre-seed/seed investors live and die at inception. That hyperfocus is our entire domain. Multi-stage funds operate on a completely different playbook. Very few can authentically span the full spectrum from Day 0 to exit (a16z as an example of a partnership that pulls this off via an operator-heavy GP roster).
- Growing up playing competitive tennis, my first coach completely sharpened my foundational game. When I started playing higher-level tournaments, he surprisingly referred me to a specialized coach. Venture is identical: founders should pair with investors whose superpower matches the exact stage they are in right now. 

Back to work people.

Global supply chains, on TRAC(k)

The United States imported $3.4 trillion of goods in 2025. The @SCANAssociation helps secure the supply chains behind around 40% of US imports.

SCAN's members include @Costco, @Walmart, @Target, and @HomeDepot and many of them buy from the same factories. Instead of each importer auditing the same factory against the same US customs security criteria (CTPAT), they share the audit reports. 

In 2025 alone, SCAN members avoided 10,159 duplicate factory audits this way, across 93 countries.

The audits are secured on the @origin_trail Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG):
→ Each audit result and factory credential becomes a tamper-evident record that can be checked at the source
→ Members and US Customs and Border Protection can check a factory's audit history without one central database owning it
→ Access stays permissioned, so sensitive audit data reaches only those entitled to see it

One audit, verified once, trusted across the network. The same pattern fits any industry where the same compliance evidence is requested again and again.

author: RockawayX
quoted_text:
Excited to have participated in the @AntSeed Foundation's $2.4M token round!

Decentralized inference is increasingly finding product market fit as several trends converge: open-source model quality, inference commoditization, agentic demand, privacy, and stablecoin native payments.

One of the most important shifts is the state of open-source AI models. Frontier labs still lead at the absolute edge, but open-source models are increasingly competitive across a much broader portion of the capability curve. That will change where value accrues. As model performance converges, distribution, inference cost, latency, privacy, and routing become increasingly important.

In the future, I see two dominant product experiences:

1. Vertically integrated products built around a specific customer need, with deep attention to UX.
2. Inference marketplaces that compete primarily across cost, latency, privacy, reliability, and routing.

In the 2nd product category, the same model can be served by many providers using different hardware, geographies, and cost structures. The logical end state is a marketplace that dynamically routes demand to the best available supply. This is where, in my opinion, AntSeed is incredibly well positioned. Going forward, cost will matter much more as companies and users increasingly prioritize ROI rather than productivity at any cost. For a consumer making 20 prompts per day, the difference between inference providers may be negligible. For an agent making millions of calls, it becomes one of the primary economic variables. AI agents should be extremely price sensitive consumers of compute. This is the core of the @AntSeed thesis.

AntSeed creates a permissionless market where inference buyers can route across competing providers based on price, performance, reputation, and privacy, rather than being locked into a single centralized API. Supply becomes more fungible and competition moves to the inference layer.

Furthermore, privacy is significantly overlooked as a key input of AI adoption. AI is increasingly where users put their most sensitive information: health data, proprietary code, investment research, financial data, internal documents, and other highly personal information. Yet most AI usage today still requires users to identify themselves to a centralized intermediary. AntSeed approaches this differently. No central account or email is required. Requests are routed P2P, and users can select TEE-verified providers where prompts remain protected from the inference provider itself. As AI becomes embedded more deeply into our workflows, I expect privacy and anonymity to move from niche preferences to core product attributes. We have already seen evidence of this with the rapid growth of Venice as a privacy-focused consumer AI product.

Then there is the question of payments. Crypto is very well suited to coordinate this market. You need permissionless, global, machine-to-machine settlement, coordinating according to reputation and economic incentives across counterparties that do not know or trust each other. Stablecoins make sub-cent, cross-border AI transactions practical in a way traditional payment rails do not.

AntSeed is already live, supports hundreds of models, has thousands of users and has demonstrated paid demand. The team combines deep crypto-native experience with the technical expertise required to build a real-time inference marketplace. I have worked with Amos and Shahaf since nearly the very inception of Antseed and have seen first hand their crystal clear focus, strong attention to solving user pain points, and non-stop shipping.  Frontier capable open-source models should create an increasingly competitive inference market.  In turn, a meaningful portion of the value will shift away from owning a proprietary model and toward efficiently coordinating compute supply and demand for inference. That is the market @AntSeed is building for.  

Very excited to be backing this team and vision.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:

A top bitcoin researcher, who actively works at the Ethereum foundation, is telling us to move our crypto to a bunker.

He thinks there is now a reasonable possibility that superhuman AI discovers a way to break the cryptography securing Bitcoin and Ethereum before quantum computers do.

That sounds insane, but there’s some important context.

Bitcoin and Ethereum rely heavily on ECDSA. At a very basic level, your wallet has a private key, and mathematics allows you to derive a public key from it.

Going forward is easy.
Going backward and figuring out the private key from the public information is considered effectively impossible.

A huge amount of crypto security rests on that assumption.

Drake is worried that AI could discover some completely new mathematical shortcut that changes it.

Why is he worried about this now?

AI has made some pretty ridiculous advances in mathematics this year.

Earlier this year, an OpenAI model autonomously disproved a famous Erdős conjecture dating back around 80 years, using mathematical techniques researchers hadn’t expected.

Then, literally the day before Drake made this post, OpenAI released hundreds of AI-generated mathematical results across hundreds of problem families.

One of those results broke through a longstanding assumption involving the complexity of integer multiplication.

That does NOT mean AI broke ECDSA.

It didn’t.
The signal is that AI is increasingly demonstrating an ability to find novel approaches to mathematical problems humans have studied for decades.

At the same time, researchers have been making progress on the other threat: quantum computers.

Estimates for the resources required to attack elliptic-curve cryptography have fallen significantly, and researchers, including Drake himself, have been working on making those attacks more efficient.

So his concern is basically:
What if everyone is preparing for quantum computers to eventually break ECDSA, but superhuman AI discovers a mathematical shortcut first?

That’s the part he thinks the crypto industry isn't sufficiently prepared for.

If ECDSA were efficiently broken, the consequences could obviously be catastrophic. Depending on the attack and what information an address has exposed, an attacker could potentially recover private keys and steal funds.

Drake isn't saying this has happened.
He isn't even saying it's definitely going to happen.

He's saying that recent AI progress has moved the probability from something he could comfortably ignore to something worth preparing for.

His recommendation is surprisingly simple.

If you're a major holder, exchange, custodian, ETF, treasury, etc., consider moving assets from heavily used addresses into fresh addresses that have never signed a transaction.

Then don't use those addresses.

That limits the cryptographic information you've exposed and potentially buys you additional protection if a vulnerability is suddenly discovered.

For the really large players, he thinks the industry should begin preparing to move beyond ECDSA entirely and toward post-quantum / hash-based cryptography.

The downside is enormous, the precautions are relatively cheap, and AI progress is moving fast enough that waiting until an attack exists may be too late.

He thinks it's now reasonable to consider the possibility that ECDSA could break before AGI/Q-Day, potentially on a timeline of months rather than years.

Nothing publicly known can currently do this.
But his argument is essentially:

For decades we've protected trillions of dollars with mathematical problems because humans couldn't figure out how to solve them efficiently.

We're now building machines that may become much better at mathematics than humans.

Maybe it's time to stop assuming those two facts can coexist forever.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: pixelarthur
quoted_text:
Robinhood Chain being “dead” is more about a lack of investable products and consumer applications that go beyond memecoins, less so attributed towards being “just another chain” with no growth potential.

Previous cycles produced insane returns from multibillion-dollar runners purely off the wow effect of bleeding-edge technology being sold to an audience that assumed it to be the epitome of crypto. Layer 2s and 3s that scaled Ethereum that much further garnered insane premiums simply because their innovations *felt* important.

In 2026, that game is solved. We understand far more about the limitations, or lack thereof, of the chains we want to build on. The next game is producing useful products that generate cash flows and actually accrue that value to the underlying token, all based upon the narratives that Robinhood as a business actually cares about.

Robinhood can be summed up into three main narratives: Agentic trading through Robinhood MCP, tokenized stocks with real utility(beyond pairing them with memecoins), and perps through Robinhood's trading products. Each narrative, while seemingly different, draws from the same impetus: that Robinhood wants to control all trading, and broader finance as a whole. 

Agentic Trading on Robinhood has already been quietly taking off. By July 29, nearly 100,000 customers had opened Agentic Trading accounts, with over $100M in assets under custody, only two months after launch. The question now is how much of that brokerage demand translates into useful onchain applications, and who will build them.

It’s an interesting spot given we know Robinhood’s playbook, yet there is no investable tokens or products on the chain that captures the opportunity. It’s entirely possible that the current “leaders” are just imposters, placeholders before the real Robinhood cycle arrives, led by applications that produce value and compete in games that haven’t already been solved.

Godspeed @optimist

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
The real fun starts when BlackRock realizes that BTC is, in fact, tokenized compute.

BTC proof of work tokens = transferable proof of compute expended in the past.

AI inference tokens = digital representation of compute to be consumed in the future.

So an AI can accumulate BTC representing past compute, then spend it to purchase future compute.

Past compute becomes future AI agency.

Which means AI agency is constrained by compute costs at both ends of this stack.

On one end, there must be enough inference compute available in GPUs and AI chips to execute the action.

On the other, there must be enough BTC available to pay for that compute and everything else the AI needs to act.

BTC can serve as that stockpile. It is the geopolitically neutral asset and network for that exact task.

The business world already understands the first constraint. AI chips are massively oversubscribed because everyone understands that access to inference compute determines AI capability.

What almost nobody understands yet is the second constraint.

BTC is not understood as critical AI infrastructure yet because the market still categorizes it as "crypto" or "blockchain" tech thanks to years of tangential gambling shitcoinery 

It has not yet priced Bitcoin as infrastructure for metering, budgeting, and imposing costs on machine agency.

Available inference compute determines what an AI can do.

Available BTC will determine how much AI can afford to do.

And the latter is a lot more scarce and valuable than the former.

If AI security ultimately comes down to:
1. controlling access to compute, and
2. imposing costs on autonomous action,

then Bitcoiners are already sitting on the world's largest infrastructure for the second half of that equation.

The world understands why AI needs chips.

It has not yet figured out why AI may need Bitcoin.

When the market finally understands that distinction, the correction is going to be insane.

text:
say you're about to pay a contributor's wallet. it's on no sanctions list, but two transfers back it got funds from an address @arkham attributes to Lazarus Group

a list check passes it, because all it asks is whether one address is in a set

after the $1.5bn Bybit theft in February 2025 the FBI asked exchanges and DeFi services to block transactions "with or derived from" the laundering addresses. derived describes a path

checking a path means choosing what counts

how many transfers away is too close? does a few cents taint a wallet? is an exchange in the middle a link or a dead end?

two teams can answer these differently and both be reasonable, so the rule shouldn't be fixed in the product

on Newton Protocol it isn't. a policy is a rule plus the data it reads, anyone can write one, and Newton operators run it, reach a quorum and sign the result. the attestation is public on Newton Explorer

Lazarus Scan is a testnet demo of this. the data is a scanner built on addresses Arkham attributes to Lazarus, the rule is a hop count. one policy flags wallets one transfer from Lazarus, another allows three. same payment passes or fails on that setting alone

Try the demo: https://t.co/T0HMLls4r9
