Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Huge congratulations to @NousResearch and team @dillonrolnick @Teknium @karan4d @theemozilla @gradyacc and many others on closing their $90M Series B at a $1.5B valuation. @Delphi_Ventures co-led their seed round, doubled down in their Series A, and participated again here. This marks us tripling down on Nous.

Following Nous' journey over the past few years has recalibrated my view of top tier founders

The team has always been months to years ahead at every juncture. They did synthetic model evaluations years before people got sick of benchmark maxing, distributed training runs before it was interesting, YARN to massively increase context length back when you couldn't dump endless text into LLMs and millions of downloads for their fine tuned Hermes Models. There were also a lot of fun projects along the way like WorldSim (massive world simulation) and FORGE.

Fast forward to today and there are 24M+ downloads of Hermes Agent since February, #1 among apps on OpenRouter by daily token usage, and 250,000+ GitHub stars along with just mass virality. The Nous team estimates Hermes drives approximately 2.5% of all global token usage.

Nous has created two things that I think are both foundational and sticky

First, Nous created a religion and an authentic cult like following. They achieved this through grassroots interest and involvement from their community and users, and by actually embracing them. A recurring example is Teknium replying to users at all hours of the day, working with them and integrating their pull requests into Hermes agent. The project’s ethos is open source and against a totalitarian end state where a room full of folks controls AI and reality itself, and that resonates globally.

The second reason is that Hermes agent unlocks a fundamental new spot on the AI optimization frontier as the open source non lab owned option. Every major competitor is owned by an AI lab (Muse owned by Meta, OpenClaw by OpenAI, Grok by SpaceX, Instinct which is closed source). With Hermes Agent you own everything you create around an AI model so you have that as a long term evolving asset (Business or personal) instead of getting IP farmed

Also with Hermes agent you can drive differentiated outcomes versus using the same model as everyone else. Individuals and businesses have a comprehensive set of owned depth around the model (Evaluations, memory, interactions, data, private IP, variety of open or closed or fine tuned models, and more). This lends itself to an AI agent that grows with you that you own for life. 

Both @satyanadella and @PalantirTech’s have shared this view that corporations don’t want to give away their IP anymore and be farmed. They want to own it as an asset.

I’ve shared my full thesis on this concept of owning vs renting your intelligence here: https://t.co/cW05wedLRD

Hermes Agent is not just a random spark, it’s the result of a team that has spent years building products, building systems and being fully enveloped in the AI world. The thousands of micro decisions and the culmination of the team led to Hermes Agent.

So what comes next? 

When you have tens of millions of users already, they can become the champions within a business to bring their Hermes build to all employees of a company. They can start sharing skills, interactions, interop, data and more and build something truly multiplayer for enterprise. 

Having Nvidia, Microsoft and Samsung as investors doubles as enabling them to be extremely smart in potentially onboarding a massive enterprise user base to Hermes Enterprise. This isn't just private businesses using Hermes internally; it's Fortune 500 companies who can offer customized and unique agents to their customers and users built on Hermes Enterprise. 

Hermes' agent was not built to be a casual or fleeting personal agent and this lends itself to a larger business expansion. 

As Teknium shared 

“I fully intend and have plainly stated many times that I always built hermes to be the most powerful AI Agent. "Normie" consumers can leverage that and we do what we can to make it an experience they can approach (the mobile app will be almost exclusively focused on consumer) - but they are not our only demographic. I want the scientists, the cybersecurity engineers, the developers, the knowledge workers, the creatives, and everyone else to be able to have an agent that they can leverage that is maximally useful to them too.…”

Nous has captured the hearts and minds of the smartest user base on earth and that's the wedge. 

Nous is building for a future where you have sovereignty over your AI stack. They are the center of gravity for Open source AI developers, users, investors and supporters. 

The AI discussion has been dominated by fear mongering driven by centralized labs to obtain a regulatory moat. This is very obvious. The safest path in my opinion is open source and acceleration. An entire world of agents pressure testing, building and dealing with each other aligned to the individual vs aligned to a centralized team of decision makers at a lab. Nous is the answer. Nous has now raised $158M to date to execute this vision.

Internally we have people who have built insane Hermes agent builds including @KSimback and @pierskicks. I have built an insanely deep Hermes build that takes in 40+ private and public data sources and finds me new founders to invest in, helps manage my liquid portfolio, and tracks my entire historical journey as a VC (past founders, deals, much more).

A few fun content items through the years has been our AMA with Teknium and our Podcast with Jeff 

AMA: https://t.co/XeeB8WdTEv

Podcast: https://t.co/wM6RQqHw94

Very excited for @robotventures (@tarunchitra and @rleshner) to lead the round alongside @nvidia @Microsoft @Samsung @usv (@fredwilson), @MenloVentures (@deedydas and team), @ycombinator and @1789Capital. Tarun is extremely deep on AI, inference (see his latest article) and open source and is the ideal lead investor in Nous.

Also amped for the Hermes Mobile App

Our goal at Delphi Ventures is to be the biggest supporters and investors of our portfolio companies. We are extremely excited for the future of Nous.

text:
Elysium Ecosystem: what we're building, and your questions 🏛️

First, thank you. In just a few hours, 150+ of you claimed your wallet. Every token page and every trade list now shows names, ranks and checkmarks instead of bare addresses. Elysium feels alive. 🙏

What is Elysium Ecosystem?

An independent, unofficial project. We're not affiliated with Elysium or Kinetiq. Just a small independent project that wanted one place to follow everything happening on Elysium.

What can I do on https://t.co/NZEdKR5UTa?

• See every project building on Elysium, with live stats
• Browse every token launched, sort and filter them
• Claim your wallet: name, picture (or your NFT), banner, links
• Follow other wallets and get alerted when they trade
• Collect badges and climb the ranks in Season 0
And a lot more is coming.

Is it free? Is it safe?

Yes. Claiming is a free signature: no transaction, no approval, no funds moved. We will never ask you to approve anything.
And it's not planned for you to buy anything on this site, now or later. The goal is simply to gather everything happening on Elysium in one place: find a project, check its stats, spot new tokens, filter them, all in a few seconds.

Will there be real rewards for testnet activity?

No, it's not planned. On testnet, everything is free: anyone can create unlimited wallets and fake activity in minutes. Rewarding that would only reward farmers, not real users. (Today alone, we hid 500+ bot profiles.) Season 0 is for fun, to discover the ecosystem and to test how progression feels.

What is Season 0?

A short test season. You may have noticed that people are climbing very fast: that's on purpose. We sped up progression a lot, because the testnet probably won't last long. Mainnet is currently expected around the end of October, and Season 1 will start then, with slower progression.

Do I keep anything after Season 0?

Yes, your final rank becomes a badge on your profile, to show where you stood. And testnet claimers keep their gold checkmark for good. Checkmarks after mainnet will be blue. And your Season 0 rank may also give you an XP boost to start Season 1.

How do badges and ranks work?

40 badges, most with 4 levels, and a few secret ones. Every level gives XP, and XP sets your rank, from Mortal to Olympian. The 10 verified wallets with the most XP (Olympian at least) become Elysian.

Champion of the Week & Leaderboard?

Every Monday at 00:00 UTC, the #1 in 7-day PnL becomes Champion of the Week, and top 100/50/25/10 earn the Leaderboard badge. Verified wallets only. First winner: Monday, Oct 12.

How do I claim my wallet?

Go to https://t.co/pklhdmb9S5 and connect your wallet. On mobile, open it inside your wallet's browser (MetaMask, Rabby…). Claim before mainnet to get the gold checkmark.

My profile disappeared?

We automatically hide fake and farmed accounts. If yours was hidden by mistake, DM us and we'll restore it.

Ideas or bugs?

Tell us. Your feedback shapes what comes next, like a chat under each token for verified wallets.

All values are testnet: tokens have no real value, and nothing on the site is financial advice.

👉 https://t.co/NZEdKR5UTa

THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE STORY — AND THE PEOPLE WHO NEEDED HELP

Today, I visited an elderly couple who have known me and experienced the work I did in the community over many years.
What they told me today really stayed with me!!

They told me they were extremely disappointed with the BBC and the media coverage about me.
They said they believed things were said about me that did not reflect what they had personally seen and experienced.
They also told me they had made their feelings known to the BBC, and that other people had contacted the BBC with their own concerns about the misleading coverage.
They and many others have told the BBC that their misleading story has created a lot of confusion and damage to a lot of vulnerable people who relied on my community support. 
These are their experiences and their views, and I believe they deserve to be heard.

But there is another part of this story that should never be forgotten.
Behind the headlines, arguments and social-media controversy were real people who needed real help.
According to my records, Depher fitted over 500 FREE boilers for people who needed them.
We completed thousands of emergency plumbing and heating jobs, helping make homes safe again.
We sent food support to thousands upon thousands of families across the UK.
We also provided gas and electricity support to families struggling through difficult times.
And we supported elderly, vulnerable and disabled people who needed practical household help.

We tried to do this without putting vulnerable people through unnecessary red tape and mountains of paperwork.
For someone who is elderly, disabled, vulnerable or struggling to survive, getting help quickly can make an enormous difference.
That is why I believe this story should not simply be about me.
It should be about the people!
The families who received food!
The households that received energy support!
The people who received boilers!
The homes where emergency plumbing and heating problems were made safe!
And the people who simply needed somebody to help them when they were struggling.

Since the 2024 reporting, I have continued to challenge allegations that I believe were inaccurate, and I say I have evidence supporting my position on a number of those issues.

I am not asking anyone to blindly believe me.
Look at my posted evidence.
Look at my posted records.
Listen to the people who were actually there.
And then make your own judgement.

Because whatever anyone thinks about me, one thing should not be forgotten:
There were thousands of real people behind the work.
And their experiences deserve to be heard too.

James

text:
Some thoughts on the recent Abstract shutdown:

I've criticized the blockspace play and the chain game a lot, but I think it's also important to acknowledge the other side.

Being late to a market doesn't necessarily mean you're doomed. Sometimes being one of the last players in, learning from everyone else's mistakes, and building something meaningfully different for a different problem can lead to massive success.

I think this is what Monad and MegaETH tried to do.

Google obviously wasn't the first search engine, and they still ended up dominating the market.

That said, I do think the window for launching another generic L1/L2 was probably closed 2 years ago. The problem is that I don't think most founders understood that at the time.

A big part of my criticism comes from talking to founders who wanted to launch their own chains without really understanding the growth and ecosystem side of it.

When I was selling the stack and working with RaaS providers, and later in other ecosystem roles, I spoke to a lot of these founders. Some of the reasons I heard for launching a new chain were completely disconnected from the actual market dynamics.

It's one thing to make a contrarian bet that everyone else thinks is stupid. It's another to make that bet without understanding why the market has moved in the direction it has.

I've spent thousands of dollars getting expert feedback and testing different directions for my own Instagram brand because I want to understand whether there's actually a market before going all-in on something.

It makes me wonder how some founders were able to raise so much money to build chains without doing the same level of market validation.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Rhino explains his ‘ball tingle’ trading style

“I would say I’m a very very pure discretionary trader and I just act on impulse. I’ve been trading for 11-12 years now, there’s certain patterns you recognize whether that's a news trade or a sentiment shift"

"My favorite type of trade that has made me most of my money is when the market has an overarching narrative that it's focused on"

"For example, when the tariff scare was going on, everyone was focused on what Trump was saying and he was just saying more and more ludicrous numbers. Obviously the markets started reacting to that, and then once the market dipped enough, you started to see the sentiment shift in the people who didn't believe the tariffs were going to be a big deal, to then believing we were going into a Great Depression. That's when I started to get into longs"

"It was similar to the Iran war where there was escalation after escalation, and then Trump started to say he was going to nuke Iran off the face of the Earth and people were somewhat taking that seriously. So, you had two scenarios where he could nuke a country of 90 million people and if that happens we have far bigger issues or he has no more rhetoric so the market really isn't going to react further to the downside"

"I like when there is one narrative the markets focusing on and then taking the other side of that"

what does a headless / agent-native professional social network look like?

likely involves some version of:

- I connect my personal agent (@Muse, Instinct, @bot ), it automatically builds out / updates / validates my profile based on it's knowledge of me and ability to search the internet;

- my agent asks me / I tell it who I want to meet, what I'm working on, and where i can help. Accepting/passing on various opportunities is stored as data to reinforce and specify these preferences.

- If directed, it can proactively find people whose interests and intentions overlap with mine; and (maybe more importantly) acts as a gate-keeper to other people's agents who want to connect with me.

quoted_text:
We started Smart Strategies to provide investors with the tools needed to design, deploy and manage their onchain investments.

Today, you can easily find thousands of yield opportunities, but understanding one well enough to make an investment decision requires answering some hard questions:

Where does the yield come from? Is it sustainable? What risks are you exposed to? Who can change the rules? What happens when something breaks?

Getting to a well-informed decision involves a combination of developing in-house expertise and relying on someone else’s judgment. 

On one end of the spectrum, a large and well capitalized fund can build an in-house crypto team and stitch together a dozen services across custody, key management, oracles, bridges, smart contracts, monitoring, risk, and execution. This costs millions of dollars and takes a long time to set up.

On the other end, a smaller fund or family office can rely on others’ judgment and choose from a pre-curated set of DeFi opportunities. This limits options and requires trusting a third party for execution and risk management, which is what their LPs might have trusted them to do in the first place.

Ultimately, many choose to not get involved at all.

There should be a third option: investors build their own strategies, understand the risks they’re exposed to, and set bounds for automatic repositioning as markets and yields move. They go from understanding an opportunity to securely deploying and managing capital, all in their control.

That’s what we’re building at Smart Strategies.

Building this requires measuring yield, quantifying risk, understanding economics, and examining governance and permissions across thousands of onchain opportunities. It’s a huge undertaking but we believe it’s the only way to deliver on the promises of onchain finance.

As institutional capital flows into stablecoins, that same capital will need to be put to work. Meanwhile, onchain financing opportunities are expanding into diverse sectors like reinsurance, GPU lending, and solar development.

As opportunities multiply and diversify, a fixed menu becomes more limiting.

We’ve spent years managing millions onchain, guiding the biggest capital allocators, handling security for major DeFi protocols including Morpho, Compound, and Euler, and selling into institutions including UBS and Goldman Sachs. We’re building all this experience into Smart Strategies.

We are not here to make DeFi look simpler than it is. We’re here to give investors the tools to handle it.

text:
For the past year or so, software engineers and coders have been warning us about the perils of AI, citing how it is doing most of their day to day jobs

Think the exact same thing is now coming to finance

Most young analysts and associates I speak with are telling me that Claude in Excel and Powerpoint is now doing at least 40-50% of the grunt work that they used to do previously

Ironically, this has actually not made work life balance any better for juniors. VPs and MDs themselves are now becoming aware of the capabilities, and chasing after new deals faster than ever before

Process timelines for deals have sped up materially, and bankers are now giving tighter timelines for investors to respond, with the assumption that investors are also using AI to speed up diligence, which has absolutely shown to be the case

The outcome seems to be a more efficient deal environment with more deals completed overall, rather than headcount reduction today

Most hiring managers, however, largely agree that new analyst class sizes should shrink moving forward. A class of 15 analysts equipped with Claude can now do the same amount of work that you would have required 18 analysts for previously

Very interesting times to live in

author: sacha
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
IMD by @surfcoderepeat wants an idea to become a working financial application through a network of AI agents.

Its bigger ambition is for those agents to earn enough to keep building, eventually supporting companies managed entirely by the network.

That starts with two connected pieces: Identity MD NFTs organise the workforce, while the $IMD token connects payments and incentives.

Each of the 2,000  NFTs represents one swarm seat* Holders connect a machine running the IMD daemon and supply AI inference, the computation behind answers and code. The NFT lets an agent contribute to the network, although owning one doesn’t guarantee profitable work.

Customers bring that workforce an objective, such as building a vault and its website. The system checks the request and breaks it into implementation, testing, review and delivery with pricing is 0.5 IMD per request, paid on @Ethereum through x402.

When that work produces a token-bearing launch, the agents can participate in its economics.

- 2% of the new token’s supply goes to wallets with accepted launch work,
- 8% is allocated per connected seat at admission.

The requester controls the remaining 90% with their value depends on what gets built and whether anyone wants it.

The same workforce can also answer oracle questions for applications.

With chain evidence, agents propose calculations at fixed blocks, and the deployer reruns the agreed calculation before signing. A contract can verify that signature and the agreement count.

POOL4 connects its trading activity to funding.

When selling pushes IMD inventory above the protocol-owned pool’s cap, excess tokens and proportional ETH are removed.

- 85% of that IMD is earmarked for burning
- 4.5% for stakers
- 6% for orchestrator bonding
- 4.5% for NFT inference nodes

Stakers receive sIMD shares with growing IMD backing. Bonding would convert reserved tokens into ETH for computation, but bonding and node payouts remain unfinished.

As of October 5, swarm deployment remains Sepolia-only, while published work includes imdUSD documentation and Ember World audits.

However, there are some concerns like shared AI mistakes, deployer-dependent signing and unaudited POOL4 contracts remain substantial risks, including documented owner powers to withdraw liquidity and sweep staked IMD.

The encouraging part is that each useful application can give people another reason to use IMD and bring more work to the swarm. If that demand becomes recurring, it could help fund the agents that build the next application.

There’s still execution ahead, but the foundation is taking shape: a workforce, a payment token and a growing set of experiments.

Turning those experiments into products people keep using would bring IMD closer to its ambition of an economy that sustains its own builders.

NFA. DYOR.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

@RedotPay led the tracked issuers, followed by @Nexo  and @ether_fi Cash.

Crypto cards payment volume has seen up-only volume since 2024. This gives a financial app recurring spending activity, and depending on the product, purchases can draw from stablecoin balances or borrowing against collateral, connecting payments with saving and credit. In other words, cards are a distribution channel for the rest of the app’s financial services.

However, payment volume alone doesn’t establish profitability. Cashback, acquisition costs, processing expenses and credit losses all affect how much value the platform retains.

I believe that the next useful comparison is how effectively issuers turn card activity into:

> retained balances
> borrowing demand
> net revenue

Usage is clearly up. However, Morpho's lending platform also saw growing usage while recording ~$11M in negative earnings over the last four quarters. Now it'll be about which crypto card issuers are able to turn growing payment volume into profitable businesses.

Today is an important day for Trump Accounts. 

When I wrote this legislation, we had a simple goal: every child in America should have the opportunity to begin life with an investment account and a stake in the extraordinary economic engine that is the United States of America.

That is why I deliberately drafted the legislation to provide for auto-enrollment—so Treasury could open accounts for all 70 million American children under the age of 18.

For children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, the federal government will make a one-time $1,000 contribution to get them started.

But the bigger idea here goes far beyond that first $1,000.

For decades, we’ve talked about how to teach young Americans the value of saving, investing, and building wealth. Trump Accounts actually gives them the tools to do it.

When a young person turns 18 and looks at an account that has been growing alongside them their entire life, capitalism is no longer an abstract concept.

They’re an investor. They’re an owner. They have skin in the game.

And my hope is that, decades from now, we look back at Trump Accounts as the beginning of an entire generation of Americans who became investors and owners from childhood.

There is incredible momentum behind these accounts, and we are seeing more and more companies pledging to contribute to their employees’ accounts, which will only continue to help the next generation of Americans.

text:
Code is getting cheaper. Judgment is not.

AI can now generate code, packages, repositories and pull requests at a scale that would have been impossible only a few years ago.

That is powerful.

It also changes the problem.

When software activity becomes cheap to generate, volume becomes a weaker signal of value. A pull request still needs to be reviewed. A package still needs context. A contributor still needs to be understood. Maintainer attention is still finite.

The question shifts from:

Can we create more?

to:

What actually deserves attention?

We saw an early version of that problem during testnet. Now it is becoming a much bigger problem across open source.

The next phase of tea is being built around that reality.

Better evidence. Better context. Better ways to separate meaningful activity from everything surrounding it.

When the noise scales, the signal has to get stronger.

The agents are racing for a fixed price. An auction does not give them one ↓

→ The price moves as people buy
→ The first person in pays whatever the price is in that moment
→ The next person pays whatever the price is by the time they arrive.

An AI agent that gets in first does not get a better price than the ones who show up later. 

The agent just buys at an earlier point on the curve.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Liquid AI just released Open d1, 2 open-weight decision models that never generate a single token. d1-3B (text + vision) and d1-omni-600M (text + image, or text + audio) read a state plus typed questions and return calibrated probabilities in 1 forward pass.

The core idea is to replace "generate JSON, then parse it" with a direct readout. Every question is a noul (P(yes)), a choice (a distribution over named options) or a score (a position on a 2 to 10 level rubric). Output tokens: always 0.

d1-3B scores 48.57 on Decision Index v0.2.1. That is the best result under 10B, and above Decider 35B-A3B (47.11), a model 12x its size. The trade-off: it trails on Knowledge (23.8 vs 33.8 for Winnow-12B). It is a decision engine, not a chat model.

Latency per question: 8 ms on RTX 4090, 16 ms on Jetson AGX Thor, 50 ms on Jetson Orin Nano. Day-one llama.cpp support......

text:
GPT-6 进入 ChatGPT 日常聊天，回答可以是一个能点、能调的智能界面

OpenAI 今天开始在 ChatGPT 推送 GPT-6，主打功能叫 Intelligent UI（智能界面）。

Plus、Pro、Business、Enterprise 用户今天起可用，免费版和 Go 版（OpenAI 的低价订阅套餐）明天开始陆续开放，ChatGPT 每周 12 亿用户都会用上。企业版能不能用，要看公司管理员的设置。

有了 Intelligent UI，GPT-6 会根据问题决定回答长什么样：对比类问题并排摆，讲原理配一张能拖动参数的示意图，简单问题照样一段文字答完。

官方举的例子是周日请朋友吃烤羊腿，人数还没定。上一代模型给的是一大段菜谱加时间表；GPT-6 给的是一张带人数调节器的购物清单，把人数从 5 改成 8，羊肉、土豆的分量跟着变，下面再接一条烹饪时间线。你也可以直接让它做个工具，比如存钱计算器、聚餐分账器，或者一个能在对话里玩的小游戏。

做法上，OpenAI 搭了一套原生界面组件库，再配一个“编译器”，模型边生成，界面边显示，不用等整段回答写完。训练时还专门评估模型做出的界面清不清楚、好不好用。

GPT-6 还能边想边答。以前用推理模型，得等它想完才出结果，现在它会先把已经想清楚的部分写出来。需要联网搜索的问题，GPT-6 Instant 平均比上一代 GPT-5.6 Instant 早 44% 开始回答。

付费用户用的是 GPT-6 Sol，免费版和 Go 版用的是 GPT-6 Luna。这两个模型 9 月 22 日已经在 Work（工作模式）、Codex（编程工具）和 API 上线，这次是补进日常聊天的 Chat 页面，Work 和 Codex 的模型不变。

Anthropic 今年 3 月 12 日给 Claude 上线了“交互式可视化”测试版，包括免费版在内的所有用户默认开启。Claude 自己判断什么时候该画图，在对话里直接生成图表、流程图、时间线，或者带滑块、按钮的小部件，比如一张能逐个点开元素的元素周期表。这个功能脱胎于 2025 年秋天的实验项目 Imagine with Claude。

两家想做的是同一件事：回答一个问题时，直接给你一个能操作的界面。区别在做法。

据报道，Claude 的可视化是模型现写的网页代码和矢量图，形式更自由，但每次都是从零画。OpenAI 用固定的组件库，模型负责挑组件、排版，样式统一，手机上原生显示，还能一块块流式出现。

OpenAI 这次还把“这题该不该用界面、用什么界面”放进了模型训练，并且和 GPT-6 一起推给所有用户。

This guy is either trolling or he genuinely does not understand quantum computing. ECDSA does not break because AI read some math papers and GPUs exist. A known break requires a fault-tolerant quantum computer running Shor's algorithm, which we do not have. To break Ethereum ECDSA, you need hundreds of thousands of physical qubits that are low-noise, controllable, connected, error-corrected, cooled, calibrated, decoded, and operated as roughly 1,200 to 1,500 logical qubits (500,000 physical qubits for error correction) for a huge Shor computation.

The missing piece is not one clever AI-discovered trick. It is an entire fault-tolerant quantum computing stack that has not been built yet. If he is claiming ECDSA falls before Q-day on GPU clusters, he is implying a classical Shor-level break of elliptic curve discrete log. Show the attack, the complexity, the benchmark, or even a toy result. Otherwise "security researcher" is doing a lot of work in his bio.

text:
Recent developments from frontier Physical AI companies are showing that robots are capable of moving from single task automation to complete workflow automation.

This unlocks a market an order of magnitude larger than single task autonomy. Similar to the jump from L3 to L4 driving automation that allowed Waymo to start scaling its operations or the jump from AI chatbots to AI agents. 

Less than 5% of physical work in the world is actually single task. Machine tending, packaging, simple assembly. A lot of work, even if seemingly repetitive, require more higher level decision making than we think.

Take for example Dyna's recent demonstration for their laundry physical agent. Addressable annual laundry labor itself is ~$9.5B. 85% of North America's 59,000 hotels have 200 rooms or fewer. These have on average one full time laundry attendant. 

That laundry attendant is continuously navigating multiple decision trees - when to load the washer, when to transfer from washer to dryer, when to fold laundry, when to move folded stacks to the shelves, etc. Correctly making these decisions requires real scene understanding, memory, and the ability to reliably execute a large number of subtasks.

A laundry attendant that has a single task folding robot still needs to be near the laundry room for most of their shift since they need to support the robot in loading, unloading, transfering stacks and moving laundry baskets.

They free up some time, but they can't effectively reallocate it to housekeeping due to the constant support required. When a robot is able to complete entire laundry workflows unattended, now the hotel manager can quickly fill a real laundry attendent hiring need with a robot or reallocate an attendant to housekeeping work.  

The ability to complete entire workflows makes robots much more useful to businesses. This is the value of physical agents.

Ethereum Just Solved a Piece of L1-L2 Fragmentation

Ethereum just hit an important milestone for its L1 + L2 ecosystem.

The Ethereum mainnet completed its first atomic transaction between L1 and L2.

In simple terms:
• L1 and L2 can coordinate in the same transaction instead of acting more like separate networks
• Less fragmentation → Apps and liquidity across different Ethereum layers can work together more easily
• Better user experience → Cross-layer actions could become faster and simpler

Why does this matter?
Ethereum has many L2s, but liquidity and users are often split across them.

Atomic composability could help make these layers feel more like one connected Ethereum ecosystem.

This is only the first step, but it could be an important piece of Ethereum’s long-term scaling roadmap.

text:
This might be the biggest opportunity blockchains have ever had. 

Technology has mostly been built around durable yet centralized trust systems. But the factors acting against these systems are getting more powerful as we near Super Intelligence™️. 

Obviously code can break due to the sheer mathematical progress AI is bringing, but less obviously, humans can be broken too. Impersonation, blackmail, and other forms of social engineering attacks are only going to get more advanced. As such, just fixing holes in code made to secure our lives is not enough, to build truly trustworthy systems of value, you will have to decentralize them and add immutability such that no single actor can, in most clear words, “not fuck it up.” This is exactly what Ethereum was built for. 

“Alright man, so what is Ethereum doing to survive this age? Are we cooked?”

Quite the contrary, the frontier is moving fast, but Ethereum is moving faster. Some quick points: 

1. The Hegotá upgrade will set the tone. 

This upgrade will make Ethereum cryptographically agile. 

EIP-8141, lovingly known as “Frames,” changes Ethereum accounts at the root level so that transaction validations can be programmable instead of tied to the ECSDA key (the thing Justin is warning people about in his post). Essentially accounts can choose how to authenticate instead of being tied to the current status quo. There are a few quantum proof signatures out there like ML-DSA and SPHINCS, with frames you can choose whatever and also be open to even more gigabrain ones to come. When you are faced with a threat, agility is key, and Hegotá sets the tone for that agility.

2. The J* upgrade will produce a MVP quantum proof L1. 

Okay, I know what you’re thinking, “why would you ever name such a consequential thing ‘I*’???What is wrong with you??” Trust me I thought this too, but I was promptly educated that names are not finalized until we get closer, in fact, the names even get a fun emoji next to them (e.g The Hegotá upgrade emoji is a goat 🐐 IFYKYK :P)

ANYWAYS

Think of J* as answering “what are the minimal changes Ethereum needs to make if quantum computers exist tomorrow?”  

The goal here is to have enough to survive Q-day. Today, this maps to achieving a PQ heartbeat on consenus layers, leanDA PQ sampling, and leanSPHINCS transactions on execution. 

TLDR: the aim is to ship this and then play Alright by Kendrick shortly after: “we gon’ be alright!” 

4. The boxes are moving in real time 

If you’ve ever seen the strawmap (a proposed roadmap for Ethereum), you’ll know it has a lot of boxes. In particular, there is a quantum box. Also fun fact: it’s literally called a strawmap because it moves as research moves, and man is it moving! 

> On August 12, leanVM was moved forward from J* to I*
> A week later, the roadmap added the minimal viable post-quantum L1 milestone to J* 

If you’re ever wondering whether Ethereum is taking this seriously, just watch the boxes and see how they dance. 

5. AI is actually HELPING

AI makes cryptographic research faster, and AI assisted formal verification means you don’t have to trust AI’s answer. Check out some of @fradamt’s posts for more. 

6. Quantum is just one threat in a much bigger battle 

You can quantum proof a bank’s system but still be fallible to the humans that run it. Ethereum tackles this from both sides, it gardens the security while also distributing the authors of the network such that there is no single point of attack.

Other blockchains, and any place that stores value TBH, will begin to claim they are quantum proof, but they fail to address the threat of being human proof too. 

7. The grand prize is here, and Ethereum can grab it. 

A neutral and secure place for ALL value, that cannot be coerced by a government, a company, or Superintelligence. 

Your life, your story, your money, can be here, forever. And many generations from now, the kids will look up and think: thank god they tried. 

Godspeed. 

Ethereum.

text:
This guy is either trolling or he genuinely does not understand quantum computing. ECDSA does not break because AI read some math papers and GPUs exist. A known break requires a fault-tolerant quantum computer running Shor's algorithm, which we do not have. To break Ethereum ECDSA, you need hundreds of thousands of physical qubits that are low-noise, controllable, connected, error-corrected, cooled, calibrated, decoded, and operated as roughly 1,200 to 1,500 logical qubits (500,000 physical qubits for error correction) for a huge Shor computation.

The missing piece is not one clever AI-discovered trick. It is an entire fault-tolerant quantum computing stack that has not been built yet. If he is claiming ECDSA falls before Q-day on GPU clusters, he is implying a classical Shor-level break of elliptic curve discrete log. Show the attack, the complexity, the benchmark, or even a toy result. Otherwise "security researcher" is doing a lot of work in his bio.
author: cryptamurai
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

After some pondering, I ended up increasing my DRV exposure today (NFA). Here's why: 

Market totally reads the headlines wrong. Partially because of redacted headlines that are plain incorrect. Jeff never said they will build onchain options themselves (my take remains correct), but appealed to builders to take a look at this market since he sees it as a massive opportunity. 

There are some cool payoff structures you can create with HIP-4 (binaries obv, capped straddles, spreads etc) and it will help hedge delta / positions on HL. 

BUT naked options and atomic multi-leg settlements aren’t feasible with HIP-4. 

I'm bullish HYPE for a multitude of reasons, but we need some type of infra upgrade to make direct competition with Derive and Paradex more viable. Can see that be HIP-5 / an infra upgrade specifically for options.

While traction is yet to be proven, Hypercall is also interesting here. With their infra, it's already possible for them to tap into HL’s OB via core writer. 

So using a workaround, it's possible to build options on top of HL without necessarily waiting for an infra upgrade. It’s currently just very annoying and traction remains to be proven. 

And the downside of Hypercall’s integration is that the option markets aren’t directly deployed on HL, so they won’t be tradable through HL’s frontend, meaning they can't tap into HL's distro. This won't change until either infra changes or HL decides to integrate them. 

Overall this is bullish for all projects currently competing in onchain options (namely Derive and Paradex) because it puts options trading at the forefront of HL traders' minds, and these products are currently the only way to trade vanilla options

today was net positive for the sector, it's great to see my onchain options thesis being validated by Jeff

author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
The two drugs that extended life in this mouse study are already prescribed to people.

Neither was designed for #ageing.

One is rapamycin, an immunosuppressant given after organ transplants. The other is trametinib, a melanoma drug sold as Mekinist.

Linda Partridge's group at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing in Cologne ran 876 mice in 4 groups: untreated controls, trametinib, rapamycin, and both drugs together. All dosing was through the food, from 6 months of age.

Trametinib alone raised median lifespan by 7-10%.

Rapamycin alone raised median lifespan by ~17%.

Together: The effects add up to 27-34%.

Combined drug treatment delayed tumour growth, and reduced brain inflammation in old female mice.

The study used 1 strain of mouse from 1 lab, with no independent replication. The researchers followed only 1 of the 3 cohorts to the end of life. The mice on rapamycin had raised blood glucose. On most of the fitness tests, the treated mice performed no differently from the controls.

Gkioni et al., 2025, Nature Aging.

This paper went through Claims this week: 15 claims, each tied to its evidence.

quoted_text:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

text:
This might be the biggest opportunity blockchains have ever had. 

Technology has mostly been built around durable yet centralized trust systems. But the factors acting against these systems are getting more powerful as we near Super Intelligence™️. 

Obviously code can break due to the sheer mathematical progress AI is bringing, but less obviously, humans can be broken too. Impersonation, blackmail, and other forms of social engineering attacks are only going to get more advanced. As such, just fixing holes in code made to secure our lives is not enough, to build truly trustworthy systems of value, you will have to decentralize them and add immutability such that no single actor can, in most clear words, “not fuck it up.” This is exactly what Ethereum was built for. 

“Alright man, so what is Ethereum doing to survive this age? Are we cooked?”

Quite the contrary, the frontier is moving fast, but Ethereum is moving faster. Some quick points: 

1. The Hegotá upgrade will set the tone. 

This upgrade will make Ethereum cryptographically agile. 

EIP-8141, lovingly known as “Frames,” changes Ethereum accounts at the root level so that transaction validations can be programmable instead of tied to the ECSDA key (the thing Justin is warning people about in his post). Essentially accounts can choose how to authenticate instead of being tied to the current status quo. There are a few quantum proof signatures out there like ML-DSA and SPHINCS, with frames you can choose whatever and also be open to even more gigabrain ones to come. When you are faced with a threat, agility is key, and Hegotá sets the tone for that agility.

2. The J* upgrade will produce a MVP quantum proof L1. 

Okay, I know what you’re thinking, “why would you ever name such a consequential thing ‘I*’???What is wrong with you??” Trust me I thought this too, but I was promptly educated that names are not finalized until we get closer, in fact, the names even get a fun emoji next to them (e.g The Hegotá upgrade emoji is a goat 🐐 IFYKYK :P)

ANYWAYS

Think of J* as answering “what are the minimal changes Ethereum needs to make if quantum computers exist tomorrow?”  

The goal here is to have enough to survive Q-day. Today, this maps to achieving a PQ heartbeat on consenus layers, leanDA PQ sampling, and leanSPHINCS transactions on execution. 

TLDR: the aim is to ship this and then play Alright by Kendrick shortly after: “we gon’ be alright!” 

4. The boxes are moving in real time 

If you’ve ever seen the strawmap (a proposed roadmap for Ethereum), you’ll know it has a lot of boxes. In particular, there is a quantum box. Also fun fact: it’s literally called a strawmap because it moves as research moves, and man is it moving! 

> On August 12, leanVM was moved forward from J* to I*
> A week later, the roadmap added the minimal viable post-quantum L1 milestone to J* 

If you’re ever wondering whether Ethereum is taking this seriously, just watch the boxes and see how they dance. 

5. AI is actually HELPING

AI makes cryptographic research faster, and AI assisted formal verification means you don’t have to trust AI’s answer. Check out some of @fradamt’s posts for more. 

6. Quantum is just one threat in a much bigger battle 

You can quantum proof a bank’s system but still be fallible to the humans that run it. Ethereum tackles this from both sides, it gardens the security while also distributing the authors of the network such that there is no single point of attack.

Other blockchains, and any place that stores value TBH, will begin to claim they are quantum proof, but they fail to address the threat of being human proof too. 

7. The grand prize is here, and Ethereum can grab it. 

A neutral and secure place for ALL value, that cannot be coerced by a government, a company, or Superintelligence. 

Your life, your story, your money, can be here, forever. And many generations from now, the kids will look up and think: thank god they tried. 

Godspeed. 

Ethereum.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
We might be massively underestimating how long AI compute stays economically useful.

6 year old 8x A100 systems are still selling for $75K–$85K, around 40% of their original ~$199K price. AI infra lenders apparently model residual value closer to 25%.

The mistake might be treating old GPUs like old phones.

An A100 doesn’t become useless when the next generation ships, the provider can downgrade it with software updates. It just gets demoted. 

Frontier training moves on, while that same compute gets recycled into inference, fine-tuning, batch jobs and cheaper regional capacity.

Microsoft ran V100s for 8.4 years against a 6 year accounting life. Sprout moved 11,664 GPUs in 13 months.

Starting to look like GPUs have a pretty long career ladder lol.

Today’s frontier hardware becomes tomorrow’s cheap inference fleet, and probably keeps earning for years after that.

"There's benefit to the receiver but there's also benefit to the giver because if you're the first person to discover someone, that's how Silicon Valley operates."
